ONIOM: HIGH_ATOMS LINK LOW_CALCULATOR. The calculator of -os is the high level on the atoms HIGH_ATOMS (1-based, ranges as 1-5,8), LOW_CALCULATOR (any calculator name, such as gfnff or lj) the low level on the whole structure; LINK is the outside atoms whose bonds to the region get hydrogen link atoms (each with its nearest atom of the region, as MultiOptPy), auto (every bond across the border, 1.2 times the covalent radii), or none. Subtractive ONIOM, E_low(real) + E_high(model) - E_low(model), with mechanical embedding or electronic embedding (-oniom_opt embedding=electronic); -oniom_middle adds a middle layer, -oniom_opt sets the link atoms, the charges, and the embedding
Perform normal vibrational analysis after converging geometry optimization.
A cutoff frequency of input value is applied to the low-frequency vibrational modes. (default: 100.0 cm^-1)
Applies frequency correction using either Truhlar's or Grimme's method. (default: grimme)
Execute normal vibrational analysis after geometry optimization, regardless of convergence status.

Detect negative eigenvalues in the Hessian matrix at ITR. 0 if you calculate exact hessian (-fc >0). If negative eigenvalues are not detected and saddle_order > 0, the optimization is stopped.

a middle layer of -oniom: ATOMS LINK CALCULATOR (as -oniom; ATOMS hold the atoms of the high layer and more): three-layer ONIOM, E_low(real) + E_middle(middle) - E_low(middle) + E_high(model) - E_middle(model)

settings of -oniom as KEY=VALUE: low.KEY=VALUE and middle.KEY=VALUE (settings of the calculator of that level, which can be any calculator of -os, an ASE calculator among them: method, basis, and its own keys as -calc_opt takes them; -func, -bs, and -calc_opt belong to the highest level and are not handed down), link (scaled, the default: the link atom at the share g = (R(Q1) + R(H)) / (R(Q1) + R(Q2)) of the bond, as Gaussian; distance: at R(Q1) + R(H) from Q1, as MultiOptPy), high_charge and high_multiplicity, middle_charge and middle_multiplicity (the model systems; by default the charge of the whole structure and its multiplicity, changed by one where the link atoms change the parity of the electrons), embedding (mechanical, the default; electronic: the higher level of every region in the charges of the atoms around it, the Coulomb energy of the model with them taken off with the lower level), charges (lowest, the default: the lowest level's, the topology charges of GFN-FF; or FILE: one per atom, in e), boundary (rc, the default: the charge of each Q2 moved to the midpoints of its bonds to the environment; zero; keep), micro (on by default: optmain, ircmain, and the chains of nebmain move the core, the outermost model region and the outer atoms of its links, and relax the rest on the lowest level (with electronic embedding the whole surface) to a minimum before every evaluation; Hessians are those of the core; the files hold the whole system; off: every atom moves), micro_mode_kill (off, the default: the environment, the low layer, is not mode-killed, the core is by its optimizer; N: the check for negative curvature of the environment after the first and every Nth relaxation, its modes followed down), micro_curvature (guided, the default: the check starts from the softest mode of the last one and takes the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxation as preconditioner; plain: from a fixed start without one), micro_precondition (lindh2007d3, the default, or another model Hessian of -modelhess, or none: its block of the environment, built at the free atoms and the fixed atoms within 4 Angstrom of the environment and shifted by micro_precondition_shift, default 1e-3 Hartree/Bohr^2, is the initial matrix of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations and the preconditioner of the curvature check; up to 16 are kept, one per structure they were built near; environments of at most 6000 variables; a relaxation that fails with it is made again without it), micro_tolerance (largest gradient component of the relaxed environment; by default micro_tolerance_factor times the thresholds of the forces of the run itself, the largest force and the RMS force of its criteria; a relaxation whose line search fails goes on with FIRE, one that ends above its tolerance says so), micro_tolerance_factor (1, the default, or a smaller share such as 0.1 of the thresholds of the forces of the run to which the environment is relaxed, not below 1e-5; up to 1), micro_check_tolerance (largest gradient component of the environment, Hartree/Bohr, for every Hessian of a check of stability: the verification of a converged saddle-point search, the start of an IRC, the stationary points of the mapper, a vibrational analysis; 1e-5 by default, never looser than the relaxations of the run; an environment that stands on a saddle point of its own is moved off it and relaxed again before any Hessian, and the error of the curvatures of a check is estimated by moving the environment to the minimum of its quadratic model and taking the Hessian again), micro_correct (on, the default, or off: correct the energy and the core gradient for the gradient left in the environment by the response of the newest Hessian of the core, where that moves the environment by at most 0.05 Bohr), micro_core_shell (Angstrom: the free atoms of the environment within that distance of the model region are moved by the optimizer with the core; by default none), micro_hessian (effective, the default: the Hessian of the relaxed surface; approximate: the same with the inverse of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations; held: the core block with the environment held), micro_hessian_solve (auto, the default: the response of the environment from its dense block, by the analytic Hessian of the lowest level or central differences of its gradient, where that costs fewer gradients than conjugate gradients and fits in the memory, conjugate gradients otherwise; dense; cg), micro_hessian_memory (GiB the Hessian of the core may take, by default half of the free memory: the analytic Hessian of the whole system where its matrices fit, central differences otherwise, refused where those do not fit either), micro_hessian_shell (Angstrom: only the environment within that distance of the core responds in the Hessian of the core, the rest is held; by default all of it), micro_optimizer (lbfgs, the default; tn: truncated Newton; or a method of -opt, for environments of at most 500 atoms), micro_coord (cart, the default; fragments: translation, rotation, and internal coordinates of each fragment of the environment), micro_predict (on or off, the default: start each relaxation from the predicted response of the environment), micro_adaptive (0, the default; ETA: the tolerance of a relaxation ETA times the largest core gradient while that is large, and a last relaxation to the full tolerance at the end), micro_replicas (1, the default: one environment; K: K replicas of the environment, each relaxed from its own environment of the core before, combined into the soft minimum -kT ln sum_k exp(-E_k / kT) of their surfaces, whose gradient is the weighted mean of theirs; not a free energy, at most kT ln K below the lowest replica; the files hold the lowest replica and NAME_replicas.xyz all of them), micro_replica_temperature (K of the soft minimum, 298.15 by default), micro_replica_start (perturb, the default: every free atom of the first relaxed environment moved by micro_replica_amplitude, 0.05 Angstrom, in a random direction of seed micro_replica_seed, 1; md: after micro_replica_md_steps, 200, steps of molecular dynamics of the environment at the temperature with the core held; files: the environments of the last K whole structures of micro_replica_files, such as the NAME_replicas.xyz of a run with replicas), traj_high_only (on or off, default off: write only the real high-layer atoms to optimization, MD and mapper XYZ trajectories)

test the SCF solution for instabilities every N evaluations and go on from a stabler one where it is unstable, repeating the evaluation there (0, the default: never; programs with an SCF that can test it, such as PySCF; the others say so once)

with -stability: an instability towards another kind of wavefunction (restricted to unrestricted): report (the default: it is said, the kind is kept), switch (go on with the unrestricted kind for the rest of the run), off (not tested)

how many structures are calculated at the same time where a command has several that do not depend on each other (the images of a chain, the two structures of a search between two structures, the states of a function of several states): the threads of the command for the built-in calculators, copies in worker processes for the calculators of the Python side. -core stays the threads of one calculation (0: as many structures at a time as -core has threads for the built-in calculators, one for those of the Python side)

an excited state (-es N, the states of -mf) is the state that was number N at the first structure and is followed from structure to structure by the overlaps of its amplitudes, instead of the state number N in the order of the energies at every structure (calculators that hand out their states: the built-in GFN0-xTB and PySCF with a restricted reference; a state that is not found again with certainty is reported)

file with the Hessian the run starts from (Cartesian, Hartree/Bohr^2): a NumPy file, an ORCA .hess file, a Gaussian .fchk file or output, or numbers only (the square or its lower triangle); the first Hessian that is asked for is taken from it

xyz file of displacements (any length): a transition-state search (-order 1) takes the Hessian mode closest to it uphill and then tracks that mode by overlap, instead of the lowest mode (RS-I-RFO becomes its mode-following variant mf_rsirfo_*); for example the tangent of a chain at the image it starts from; Cartesian coordinates

coordinate system of the optimization: cart, ric, dic, tric (translation-rotation internal coordinates, delocalized), tric-p (their primitive set), tric-cart[:WEIGHT] (TRIC stacked with weighted Cartesian coordinates), spherical (every atom by r, theta, phi about the centroid), hyperspherical or polar (the whole structure by its distance from the centroid and 3N-1 angles; hyperspherical:FILE about the structure of FILE; for optimizations, not chains), auto (tric-cart, or cart for atom clusters, dense or periodic networks and very large systems), or a registered name. Calculators always receive Cartesian structures.

user-defined bias potentials as expressions of geometric variables in atomic units (energy in Hartree), e.g. '0.15*(dist(1,2)-1.5*ang)^2'; functions dist, angle, dihedral, oop, x, y, z with atoms or groups [1-3]; see the bias documentation

the spin state as the number of unpaired electrons 2S instead of -spin (2S + 1), as the 'spin' of PySCF, xTB's uhf, and several Rust engines count it; one value, or one per state. It sets the state only: an unrestricted reference for singlets is -u
program-specific calculator settings as key=value (Python literals), e.g. density_fit=True conv_tol=1e-10; for -os ase:module:Class they are constructor keywords

user-defined constraints as expressions in the -ubias language: 'EXPR' holds the starting value, 'EXPR = VALUE' a value (atomic units; 'ang', 'deg' convert), '; period = 2*pi' wraps angle-like functions, '; tolerance = 1e-8' holds a noisy function to that residual instead of 1e-10, e.g. 'dist(1,2) - dist(3,4)'; with -vc the functions of the cell as well, e.g. 'volume()', 'cell_a() = 10.5*ang', 'cell_a()/cell_b()'

groups of atoms (ex.) 1,2,3 4,5 whose distances to each other are held at their values in the input (MultiOptPy: 'set the gradient of internal coordinates between atoms to zero'): every distance of a group is a constraint as -pc bond is, taken out of the gradient and of the Hessian and restored after every step
CCQN reaction-coordinate axis from reactive bonds, as atom pairs (ex.) 1,2 3,4
CCQN axis toward the midpoint of the straight line to this product structure (xyz)
cosine of the CCQN cone half-angle (default: 0.1 for bonds, 0.5 for a product)
CCQN uphill step and initial saddle trust radius in Angstrom (default: 0.1)
vibrations at or below this wavenumber (cm^-1) are left out of the thermochemistry

treatment of the thermal energy of low frequencies apart from that of the entropy (-freq_corr): head-gordon, truhlar, or none; without it, the one that goes with -freq_corr (grimme: head-gordon, truhlar: truhlar)
cutoff (cm^-1) of the treatment of the thermal energy; without it, -freq_cutoff
concentration (mol/L) for the translational entropy of a solute instead of the pressure of the gas
scale factor of the vibrational frequencies in the thermochemistry
scale factor of the frequencies in the zero-point energy; without it, -freq_scale
imaginary frequencies up to this magnitude (cm^-1) enter the thermochemistry as real ones
moment of inertia that bounds the free rotor of -freq_corr grimme: global (1e-44 kg m^2) or molecule (the mean moment of the molecule)
distance (Bohr) within which atoms coincide in the point-group analysis
vibrational analysis: project the direction of the gradient out with the rigid-body motions (the modes orthogonal to a reaction path at a point that is not stationary)

after a converged optimization, the derivatives in every constant of the bias options (a force constant, an equilibrium value, the AFIR collision energy, ...; per unit of the option as it is written): of the bias energy, and how the stationary point and its energy without the bias move with the constant (dx/dp = -H^+ dg/dp with the Hessian of the whole surface); written to bias_derivatives.csv and the log

-mf opt_meci: do not check the branching plane with gradients at displaced structures when the search has converged (the check costs four evaluations of both states and sends the search on if the point is not stationary on the seam)

-mf opt_mesx, -mf opt_meci: what a step is judged by when the trust radius is adapted: energy (the change of the mean energy of the two states against the quadratic model of the projected gradient, as for a search on one surface) or merit (the change of the function the projected gradient belongs to: the mean energy within the seam and (E1 - E2)^2 / |g1 - g2|)

optimize the cell together with the atoms (cells periodic in three directions; the stress comes from the calculator, or from differences of the energy where it has none); with -es the stress of that state, with -mf the two states combined in the variables of the cell (their enthalpies and their gradients in the variables: crossing points and conical intersections with the cell)
-vc: external pressure in GPa; the enthalpy E + P V is minimized

-vc: artificial force on the cell (periodic AFIR): pairs of a collision energy in kJ/mol (positive: compress, negative: expand; a ramp as for -ma) and the distances it acts on, a list of a, b, c (origin to the tip of a lattice vector) and ab, bc, ca (between two tips), e.g. -vc_afir 200 a,b -vc_afir -100 ab

-vc: hard constraints on the cell, comma-separated, at the values of the input or NAME=VALUE: a, b, c (lengths, Angstrom), alpha, beta, gamma (degrees), volume (Angstrom^3; only the shape relaxes), shape (b/a, c/a and the three angles; only an isotropic scaling relaxes), a_vector, b_vector, c_vector (the three Cartesian components of a lattice vector, e.g. the normal vector of a slab), ax, ay, ..., cz (one component, Angstrom); the same constraints as -uc 'cell_a()', 'volume()', ...; e.g. -vc_fix volume, -vc_fix c_vector, -vc_fix a=10.5,gamma

-irc: further settings of the IRC as KEY=VALUE: first_step (check, the default: test the first point of each side and replace it by the energy minimum on a hypersphere around the transition state when it fails; off: MultiOptPy's first point), angle (largest angle in degrees between the downhill direction at the first point and the transition vector, 10), rho_min and rho_max (limits of actual over predicted energy change of the first step, 0.75 and 1.25), initial (mass-weighted length of the displacement from the transition state, 0.1 of the step size), sides (both, forward, backward), masses (standard: atomic weights, as the vibrational analysis; isotope: the most abundant isotopes, as MultiOptPy), energy_rise (retry, the default: a step that raised the energy is taken again at half its length, LQA and Euler; stop: end a side where the energy rises; off: keep such points, as MultiOptPy), overshoot (retry, the default, with energy_rise=retry: a step whose end has a gradient that points back along it is taken again at half its length; keep: such points stay), bend (off, the default; a share such as 0.25: no step is longer than the one that loses this share of the energy it gains by cutting the bend of the valley, from the curvature of the path and the Hessian across it; for exact Hessians along the path, -fc 1), approach (on, the default: below the force thresholds a side goes on to the minimum until the gradient is below approach_max_force and approach_rms_force, LQA, Euler, RK4; off: end at the first point below the thresholds, as MultiOptPy), approach_max_force (0.000015), approach_rms_force (0.00001), approach_steps (100), max_force (0.0004), rms_force (0.0001), min_points (10), oscillations (5), sphere_iterations (30), sphere_gradient (1e-4), sphere_step (1e-3)

ONIOM: HIGH_ATOMS LINK LOW_CALCULATOR. The calculator of -os is the high level on the atoms HIGH_ATOMS (1-based, ranges as 1-5,8), LOW_CALCULATOR (any calculator name, such as gfnff or lj) the low level on the whole structure; LINK is the outside atoms whose bonds to the region get hydrogen link atoms (each with its nearest atom of the region, as MultiOptPy), auto (every bond across the border, 1.2 times the covalent radii), or none. Subtractive ONIOM, E_low(real) + E_high(model) - E_low(model), with mechanical embedding or electronic embedding (-oniom_opt embedding=electronic); -oniom_middle adds a middle layer, -oniom_opt sets the link atoms, the charges, and the embedding

a middle layer of -oniom: ATOMS LINK CALCULATOR (as -oniom; ATOMS hold the atoms of the high layer and more): three-layer ONIOM, E_low(real) + E_middle(middle) - E_low(middle) + E_high(model) - E_middle(model)

settings of -oniom as KEY=VALUE: low.KEY=VALUE and middle.KEY=VALUE (settings of the calculator of that level, which can be any calculator of -os, an ASE calculator among them: method, basis, and its own keys as -calc_opt takes them; -func, -bs, and -calc_opt belong to the highest level and are not handed down), link (scaled, the default: the link atom at the share g = (R(Q1) + R(H)) / (R(Q1) + R(Q2)) of the bond, as Gaussian; distance: at R(Q1) + R(H) from Q1, as MultiOptPy), high_charge and high_multiplicity, middle_charge and middle_multiplicity (the model systems; by default the charge of the whole structure and its multiplicity, changed by one where the link atoms change the parity of the electrons), embedding (mechanical, the default; electronic: the higher level of every region in the charges of the atoms around it, the Coulomb energy of the model with them taken off with the lower level), charges (lowest, the default: the lowest level's, the topology charges of GFN-FF; or FILE: one per atom, in e), boundary (rc, the default: the charge of each Q2 moved to the midpoints of its bonds to the environment; zero; keep), micro (on by default: optmain, ircmain, and the chains of nebmain move the core, the outermost model region and the outer atoms of its links, and relax the rest on the lowest level (with electronic embedding the whole surface) to a minimum before every evaluation; Hessians are those of the core; the files hold the whole system; off: every atom moves), micro_mode_kill (off, the default: the environment, the low layer, is not mode-killed, the core is by its optimizer; N: the check for negative curvature of the environment after the first and every Nth relaxation, its modes followed down), micro_curvature (guided, the default: the check starts from the softest mode of the last one and takes the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxation as preconditioner; plain: from a fixed start without one), micro_precondition (lindh2007d3, the default, or another model Hessian of -modelhess, or none: its block of the environment, built at the free atoms and the fixed atoms within 4 Angstrom of the environment and shifted by micro_precondition_shift, default 1e-3 Hartree/Bohr^2, is the initial matrix of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations and the preconditioner of the curvature check; up to 16 are kept, one per structure they were built near; environments of at most 6000 variables; a relaxation that fails with it is made again without it), micro_tolerance (largest gradient component of the relaxed environment; by default micro_tolerance_factor times the thresholds of the forces of the run itself, the largest force and the RMS force of its criteria; a relaxation whose line search fails goes on with FIRE, one that ends above its tolerance says so), micro_tolerance_factor (1, the default, or a smaller share such as 0.1 of the thresholds of the forces of the run to which the environment is relaxed, not below 1e-5; up to 1), micro_check_tolerance (largest gradient component of the environment, Hartree/Bohr, for every Hessian of a check of stability: the verification of a converged saddle-point search, the start of an IRC, the stationary points of the mapper, a vibrational analysis; 1e-5 by default, never looser than the relaxations of the run; an environment that stands on a saddle point of its own is moved off it and relaxed again before any Hessian, and the error of the curvatures of a check is estimated by moving the environment to the minimum of its quadratic model and taking the Hessian again), micro_correct (on, the default, or off: correct the energy and the core gradient for the gradient left in the environment by the response of the newest Hessian of the core, where that moves the environment by at most 0.05 Bohr), micro_core_shell (Angstrom: the free atoms of the environment within that distance of the model region are moved by the optimizer with the core; file with the Hessian the run starts from (Cartesian, Hartree/Bohr^2): a NumPy file, an ORCA .hess file, a Gaussian .fchk file or output, or numbers only (the square or its lower triangle); the first Hessian that is asked for is taken from it

xyz file of displacements (any length): a transition-state search (-order 1) takes the Hessian mode closest to it uphill and then tracks that mode by overlap, instead of the lowest mode (RS-I-RFO becomes its mode-following variant mf_rsirfo_*); for example the tangent of a chain at the image it starts from; Cartesian coordinates

coordinate system of the optimization: cart, ric, dic, tric (translation-rotation internal coordinates, delocalized), tric-p (their primitive set), tric-cart[:WEIGHT] (TRIC stacked with weighted Cartesian coordinates), spherical (every atom by r, theta, phi about the centroid), hyperspherical or polar (the whole structure by its distance from the centroid and 3N-1 angles; hyperspherical:FILE about the structure of FILE; for optimizations, not chains), auto (tric-cart, or cart for atom clusters, dense or periodic networks and very large systems), or a registered name. Calculators always receive Cartesian structures.

user-defined bias potentials as expressions of geometric variables in atomic units (energy in Hartree), e.g. '0.15*(dist(1,2)-1.5*ang)^2'; functions dist, angle, dihedral, oop, x, y, z with atoms or groups [1-3]; see the bias documentation

the spin state as the number of unpaired electrons 2S instead of -spin (2S + 1), as the 'spin' of PySCF, xTB's uhf, and several Rust engines count it; one value, or one per state. It sets the state only: an unrestricted reference for singlets is -u
program-specific calculator settings as key=value (Python literals), e.g. density_fit=True conv_tol=1e-10; for -os ase:module:Class they are constructor keywords

user-defined constraints as expressions in the -ubias language: 'EXPR' holds the starting value, 'EXPR = VALUE' a value (atomic units; 'ang', 'deg' convert), '; period = 2*pi' wraps angle-like functions, '; tolerance = 1e-8' holds a noisy function to that residual instead of 1e-10, e.g. 'dist(1,2) - dist(3,4)'; with -vc the functions of the cell as well, e.g. 'volume()', 'cell_a() = 10.5*ang', 'cell_a()/cell_b()'

groups of atoms (ex.) 1,2,3 4,5 whose distances to each other are held at their values in the input (MultiOptPy: 'set the gradient of internal coordinates between atoms to zero'): every distance of a group is a constraint as -pc bond is, taken out of the gradient and of the Hessian and restored after every step
CCQN reaction-coordinate axis from reactive bonds, as atom pairs (ex.) 1,2 3,4
CCQN axis toward the midpoint of the straight line to this product structure (xyz)
cosine of the CCQN cone half-angle (default: 0.1 for bonds, 0.5 for a product)
CCQN uphill step and initial saddle trust radius in Angstrom (default: 0.1)
vibrations at or below this wavenumber (cm^-1) are left out of the thermochemistry

treatment of the thermal energy of low frequencies apart from that of the entropy (-freq_corr): head-gordon, truhlar, or none; without it, the one that goes with -freq_corr (grimme: head-gordon, truhlar: truhlar)
cutoff (cm^-1) of the treatment of the thermal energy; without it, -freq_cutoff
concentration (mol/L) for the translational entropy of a solute instead of the pressure of the gas
scale factor of the vibrational frequencies in the thermochemistry
scale factor of the frequencies in the zero-point energy; without it, -freq_scale
imaginary frequencies up to this magnitude (cm^-1) enter the thermochemistry as real ones
moment of inertia that bounds the free rotor of -freq_corr grimme: global (1e-44 kg m^2) or molecule (the mean moment of the molecule)
distance (Bohr) within which atoms coincide in the point-group analysis
vibrational analysis: project the direction of the gradient out with the rigid-body motions (the modes orthogonal to a reaction path at a point that is not stationary)

after a converged optimization, the derivatives in every constant of the bias options (a force constant, an equilibrium value, the AFIR collision energy, ...; per unit of the option as it is written): of the bias energy, and how the stationary point and its energy without the bias move with the constant (dx/dp = -H^+ dg/dp with the Hessian of the whole surface); written to bias_derivatives.csv and the log

-mf opt_meci: do not check the branching plane with gradients at displaced structures when the search has converged (the check costs four evaluations of both states and sends the search on if the point is not stationary on the seam)

-mf opt_mesx, -mf opt_meci: what a step is judged by when the trust radius is adapted: energy (the change of the mean energy of the two states against the quadratic model of the projected gradient, as for a search on one surface) or merit (the change of the function the projected gradient belongs to: the mean energy within the seam and (E1 - E2)^2 / |g1 - g2|)

optimize the cell together with the atoms (cells periodic in three directions; the stress comes from the calculator, or from differences of the energy where it has none); with -es the stress of that state, with -mf the two states combined in the variables of the cell (their enthalpies and their gradients in the variables: crossing points and conical intersections with the cell)
-vc: external pressure in GPa; the enthalpy E + P V is minimized

-vc: artificial force on the cell (periodic AFIR): pairs of a collision energy in kJ/mol (positive: compress, negative: expand; a ramp as for -ma) and the distances it acts on, a list of a, b, c (origin to the tip of a lattice vector) and ab, bc, ca (between two tips), e.g. -vc_afir 200 a,b -vc_afir -100 ab

-vc: hard constraints on the cell, comma-separated, at the values of the input or NAME=VALUE: a, b, c (lengths, Angstrom), alpha, beta, gamma (degrees), volume (Angstrom^3; only the shape relaxes), shape (b/a, c/a and the three angles; only an isotropic scaling relaxes), a_vector, b_vector, c_vector (the three Cartesian components of a lattice vector, e.g. the normal vector of a slab), ax, ay, ..., cz (one component, Angstrom); the same constraints as -uc 'cell_a()', 'volume()', ...; e.g. -vc_fix volume, -vc_fix c_vector, -vc_fix a=10.5,gamma

-irc: further settings of the IRC as KEY=VALUE: first_step (check, the default: test the first point of each side and replace it by the energy minimum on a hypersphere around the transition state when it fails; off: MultiOptPy's first point), angle (largest angle in degrees between the downhill direction at the first point and the transition vector, 10), rho_min and rho_max (limits of actual over predicted energy change of the first step, 0.75 and 1.25), initial (mass-weighted length of the displacement from the transition state, 0.1 of the step size), sides (both, forward, backward), masses (standard: atomic weights, as the vibrational analysis; isotope: the most abundant isotopes, as MultiOptPy), energy_rise (retry, the default: a step that raised the energy is taken again at half its length, LQA and Euler; stop: end a side where the energy rises; off: keep such points, as MultiOptPy), overshoot (retry, the default, with energy_rise=retry: a step whose end has a gradient that points back along it is taken again at half its length; keep: such points stay), bend (off, the default; a share such as 0.25: no step is longer than the one that loses this share of the energy it gains by cutting the bend of the valley, from the curvature of the path and the Hessian across it; for exact Hessians along the path, -fc 1), approach (on, the default: below the force thresholds a side goes on to the minimum until the gradient is below approach_max_force and approach_rms_force, LQA, Euler, RK4; off: end at the first point below the thresholds, as MultiOptPy), approach_max_force (0.000015), approach_rms_force (0.00001), approach_steps (100), max_force (0.0004), rms_force (0.0001), min_points (10), oscillations (5), sphere_iterations (30), sphere_gradient (1e-4), sphere_step (1e-3)

-mf bitss REFERENCE: settings of the binary-image transition state search as KEY=VALUE: f (reduction of the separation per stage, 0.5), alpha (10), beta (0.1), interval (iterations between two settings of the coefficients, 100), points (points between the images for the barrier estimate, 3), min_separation (Bohr, 0.01), stages (30), step_share (longest step as a share of the separation asked for, 0.5; none: no limit), midpoint_shift (end when the midpoint moved by less than this share of the reduction of a stage; none), midpoint_gradient (true)

settings of -oniom as KEY=VALUE: low.KEY=VALUE and middle.KEY=VALUE (settings of the calculator of that level, which can be any calculator of -os, an ASE calculator among them: method, basis, and its own keys as -calc_opt takes them; -func, -bs, and -calc_opt belong to the highest level and are not handed down), link (scaled, the default: the link atom at the share g = (R(Q1) + R(H)) / (R(Q1) + R(Q2)) of the bond, as Gaussian; distance: at R(Q1) + R(H) from Q1, as MultiOptPy), high_charge and high_multiplicity, middle_charge and middle_multiplicity (the model systems; by default the charge of the whole structure and its multiplicity, changed by one where the link atoms change the parity of the electrons), embedding (mechanical, the default; electronic: the higher level of every region in the charges of the atoms around it, the Coulomb energy of the model with them taken off with the lower level), charges (lowest, the default: the lowest level's, the topology charges of GFN-FF; or FILE: one per atom, in e), boundary (rc, the default: the charge of each Q2 moved to the midpoints of its bonds to the environment; zero; keep), micro (on by default: optmain, ircmain, and the chains of nebmain move the core, the outermost model region and the outer atoms of its links, and relax the rest on the lowest level (with electronic embedding the whole surface) to a minimum before every evaluation; Hessians are those of the core; the files hold the whole system; off: every atom moves), micro_mode_kill (off, the default: the environment, the low layer, is not mode-killed, the core is by its optimizer; N: the check for negative curvature of the environment after the first and every Nth relaxation, its modes followed down), micro_curvature (guided, the default: the check starts from the softest mode of the last one and takes the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxation as preconditioner; plain: from a fixed start without one), micro_precondition (lindh2007d3, the default, or another model Hessian of -modelhess, or none: its block of the environment, built at the free atoms and the fixed atoms within 4 Angstrom of the environment and shifted by micro_precondition_shift, default 1e-3 Hartree/Bohr^2, is the initial matrix of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations and the preconditioner of the curvature check; up to 16 are kept, one per structure they were built near; environments of at most 6000 variables; a relaxation that fails with it is made again without it), micro_tolerance (largest gradient component of the relaxed environment; by default micro_tolerance_factor times the thresholds of the forces of the run itself, the largest force and the RMS force of its criteria; a relaxation whose line search fails goes on with FIRE, one that ends above its tolerance says so), micro_tolerance_factor (1, the default, or a smaller share such as 0.1 of the thresholds of the forces of the run to which the environment is relaxed, not below 1e-5; up to 1), micro_check_tolerance (largest gradient component of the environment, Hartree/Bohr, for every Hessian of a check of stability: the verification of a converged saddle-point search, the start of an IRC, the stationary points of the mapper, a vibrational analysis; 1e-5 by default, never looser than the relaxations of the run; an environment that stands on a saddle point of its own is moved off it and relaxed again before any Hessian, and the error of the curvatures of a check is estimated by moving the environment to the minimum of its quadratic model and taking the Hessian again), micro_correct (on, the default, or off: correct the energy and the core gradient for the gradient left in the environment by the response of the newest Hessian of the core, where that moves the environment by at most 0.05 Bohr), micro_core_shell (Angstrom: the free atoms of the environment within that distance of the model region are moved by the optimizer with the core; by default none), micro_hessian (effective, the default: the Hessian of the relaxed surface; approximate: the same with the inverse of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations; held: the core block with the environment held), micro_hessian_solve (auto, the default: the response of the environment from its dense block, by the analytic Hessian of the lowest level or central differences of its gradient, where that costs fewer gradients than conjugate gradients and fits in the memory, conjugate gradients otherwise; dense; cg), micro_hessian_memory (GiB the Hessian of the core may take, by default half of the free memory: the analytic Hessian of the whole system where its matrices fit, central differences otherwise, refused where those do not fit either), micro_hessian_shell (Angstrom: only the environment within that distance of the core responds in the Hessian of the core, the rest is held; by default all of it), micro_optimizer (lbfgs, the default; tn: truncated Newton; or a method of -opt, for environments of at most 500 atoms), micro_coord (cart, the default; fragments: translation, rotation, and internal coordinates of each fragment of the environment), micro_predict (on or off, the default: start each relaxation from the predicted response of the environment), micro_adaptive (0, the default; ETA: the tolerance of a relaxation ETA times the largest core gradient while that is large, and a last relaxation to the full tolerance at the end), micro_replicas (1, the default: one environment; K: K replicas of the environment, each relaxed from its own environment of the core before, combined into the soft minimum -kT ln sum_k exp(-E_k / kT) of their surfaces, whose gradient is the weighted mean of theirs; not a free energy, at most kT ln K below the lowest replica; the files hold the lowest replica and NAME_replicas.xyz all of them), micro_replica_temperature (K of the soft minimum, 298.15 by default), micro_replica_start (perturb, the default: every free atom of the first relaxed environment moved by micro_replica_amplitude, 0.05 Angstrom, in a random direction of seed micro_replica_seed, 1; md: after micro_replica_md_steps, 200, steps of molecular dynamics of the environment at the temperature with the core held; files: the environments of the last K whole structures of micro_replica_files, such as the NAME_replicas.xyz of a run with replicas), traj_high_only (on or off, default off: write only the real high-layer atoms to optimization, MD and mapper XYZ trajectories)

test the SCF solution for instabilities every N evaluations and go on from a stabler one where it is unstable, repeating the evaluation there (0, the default: never; programs with an SCF that can test it, such as PySCF; the others say so once)

with -stability: an instability towards another kind of wavefunction (restricted to unrestricted): report (the default: it is said, the kind is kept), switch (go on with the unrestricted kind for the rest of the run), off (not tested)

how many structures are calculated at the same time where a command has several that do not depend on each other (the images of a chain, the two structures of a search between two structures, the states of a function of several states): the threads of the command for the built-in calculators, copies in worker processes for the calculators of the Python side. -core stays the threads of one calculation (0: as many structures at a time as -core has threads for the built-in calculators, one for those of the Python side)

an excited state (-es N, the states of -mf) is the state that was number N at the first structure and is followed from structure to structure by the overlaps of its amplitudes, instead of the state number N in the order of the energies at every structure (calculators that hand out their states: the built-in GFN0-xTB and PySCF with a restricted reference; a state that is not found again with certainty is reported)

file with the Hessian the run starts from (Cartesian, Hartree/Bohr^2): a NumPy file, an ORCA .hess file, a Gaussian .fchk file or output, or numbers only (the square or its lower triangle); the first Hessian that is asked for is taken from it

xyz file of displacements (any length): a transition-state search (-order 1) takes the Hessian mode closest to it uphill and then tracks that mode by overlap, instead of the lowest mode (RS-I-RFO becomes its mode-following variant mf_rsirfo_*); for example the tangent of a chain at the image it starts from; Cartesian coordinates

coordinate system of the optimization: cart, ric, dic, tric (translation-rotation internal coordinates, delocalized), tric-p (their primitive set), tric-cart[:WEIGHT] (TRIC stacked with weighted Cartesian coordinates), spherical (every atom by r, theta, phi about the centroid), hyperspherical or polar (the whole structure by its distance from the centroid and 3N-1 angles; hyperspherical:FILE about the structure of FILE; for optimizations, not chains), auto (tric-cart, or cart for atom clusters, dense or periodic networks and very large systems), or a registered name. Calculators always receive Cartesian structures.

user-defined bias potentials as expressions of geometric variables in atomic units (energy in Hartree), e.g. '0.15*(dist(1,2)-1.5*ang)^2'; functions dist, angle, dihedral, oop, x, y, z with atoms or groups [1-3]; see the bias documentation

the spin state as the number of unpaired electrons 2S instead of -spin (2S + 1), as the 'spin' of PySCF, xTB's uhf, and several Rust engines count it; one value, or one per state. It sets the state only: an unrestricted reference for singlets is -u
program-specific calculator settings as key=value (Python literals), e.g. density_fit=True conv_tol=1e-10; for -os ase:module:Class they are constructor keywords

user-defined constraints as expressions in the -ubias language: 'EXPR' holds the starting value, 'EXPR = VALUE' a value (atomic units; 'ang', 'deg' convert), '; period = 2*pi' wraps angle-like functions, '; tolerance = 1e-8' holds a noisy function to that residual instead of 1e-10, e.g. 'dist(1,2) - dist(3,4)'; with -vc the functions of the cell as well, e.g. 'volume()', 'cell_a() = 10.5*ang', 'cell_a()/cell_b()'

groups of atoms (ex.) 1,2,3 4,5 whose distances to each other are held at their values in the input (MultiOptPy: 'set the gradient of internal coordinates between atoms to zero'): every distance of a group is a constraint as -pc bond is, taken out of the gradient and of the Hessian and restored after every step

treatment of the thermal energy of low frequencies apart from that of the entropy (-freq_corr): head-gordon, truhlar, or none; without it, the one that goes with -freq_corr (grimme: head-gordon, truhlar: truhlar)

after a converged optimization, the derivatives in every constant of the bias options (a force constant, an equilibrium value, the AFIR collision energy, ...; per unit of the option as it is written): of the bias energy, and how the stationary point and its energy without the bias move with the constant (dx/dp = -H^+ dg/dp with the Hessian of the whole surface); written to bias_derivatives.csv and the log

-mf opt_mesx, -mf opt_meci: what a step is judged by when the trust radius is adapted: energy (the change of the mean energy of the two states against the quadratic model of the projected gradient, as for a search on one surface) or merit (the change of the function the projected gradient belongs to: the mean energy within the seam and (E1 - E2)^2 / |g1 - g2|)

optimize the cell together with the atoms (cells periodic in three directions; the stress comes from the calculator, or from differences of the energy where it has none); with -es the stress of that state, with -mf the two states combined in the variables of the cell (their enthalpies and their gradients in the variables: crossing points and conical intersections with the cell)

settings of -oniom as KEY=VALUE: low.KEY=VALUE and middle.KEY=VALUE (settings of the calculator of that level, which can be any calculator of -os, an ASE calculator among them: method, basis, and its own keys as -calc_opt takes them; -func, -bs, and -calc_opt belong to the highest level and are not handed down), link (scaled, the default: the link atom at the share g = (R(Q1) + R(H)) / (R(Q1) + R(Q2)) of the bond, as Gaussian; distance: at R(Q1) + R(H) from Q1, as MultiOptPy), high_charge and high_multiplicity, middle_charge and middle_multiplicity (the model systems; by default the charge of the whole structure and its multiplicity, changed by one where the link atoms change the parity of the electrons), embedding (mechanical, the default; electronic: the higher level of every region in the charges of the atoms around it, the Coulomb energy of the model with them taken off with the lower level), charges (lowest, the default: the lowest level's, the topology charges of GFN-FF; or FILE: one per atom, in e), boundary (rc, the default: the charge of each Q2 moved to the midpoints of its bonds to the environment; zero; keep), micro (on by default: optmain, ircmain, and the chains of nebmain move the core, the outermost model region and the outer atoms of its links, and relax the rest on the lowest level (with electronic embedding the whole surface) to a minimum before every evaluation; Hessians are those of the core; the files hold the whole system; off: every atom moves), micro_mode_kill (off, the default: the environment, the low layer, is not mode-killed, the core is by its optimizer; N: the check for negative curvature of the environment after the first and every Nth relaxation, its modes followed down), micro_curvature (guided, the default: the check starts from the softest mode of the last one and takes the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxation as preconditioner; plain: from a fixed start without one), micro_precondition (lindh2007d3, the default, or another model Hessian of -modelhess, or none: its block of the environment, built at the free atoms and the fixed atoms within 4 Angstrom of the environment and shifted by micro_precondition_shift, default 1e-3 Hartree/Bohr^2, is the initial matrix of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations and the preconditioner of the curvature check; up to 16 are kept, one per structure they were built near; environments of at most 6000 variables; a relaxation that fails with it is made again without it), micro_tolerance (largest gradient component of the relaxed environment; by default micro_tolerance_factor times the thresholds of the forces of the run itself, the largest force and the RMS force of its criteria; a relaxation whose line search fails goes on with FIRE, one that ends above its tolerance says so), micro_tolerance_factor (1, the default, or a smaller share such as 0.1 of the thresholds of the forces of the run to which the environment is relaxed, not below 1e-5; up to 1), micro_check_tolerance (largest gradient component of the environment, Hartree/Bohr, for every Hessian of a check of stability: the verification of a converged saddle-point search, the start of an IRC, the stationary points of the mapper, a vibrational analysis; 1e-5 by default, never looser than the relaxations of the run; an environment that stands on a saddle point of its own is moved off it and relaxed again before any Hessian, and the error of the curvatures of a check is estimated by moving the environment to the minimum of its quadratic model and taking the Hessian again), micro_correct (on, the default, or off: correct the energy and the core gradient for the gradient left in the environment by the response of the newest Hessian of the core, where that moves the environment by at most 0.05 Bohr), micro_core_shell (Angstrom: the free atoms of the environment within that distance of the model region are moved by the optimizer with the core; by default none), micro_hessian (effective, the default: the Hessian of the relaxed surface; approximate: the same with the inverse of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations; held: the core block with the environment held), micro_hessian_solve (auto, the default: the response of the environment from its dense block, by the analytic Hessian of the lowest level or central differences of its gradient, where that costs fewer gradients than conjugate gradients and fits in the memory, conjugate gradients otherwise; dense; cg), micro_hessian_memory (GiB the Hessian of the core may take, by default half of the free memory: the analytic Hessian of the whole system where its matrices fit, central differences otherwise, refused where those do not fit either), micro_hessian_shell (Angstrom: only the environment within that distance of the core responds in the Hessian of the core, the rest is held; by default all of it), micro_optimizer (lbfgs, the default; tn: truncated Newton; or a method of -opt, for environments of at most 500 atoms), micro_coord (cart, the default; fragments: translation, rotation, and internal coordinates of each fragment of the environment), micro_predict (on or off, the default: start each relaxation from the predicted response of the environment), micro_adaptive (0, the default; ETA: the tolerance of a relaxation ETA times the largest core gradient while that is large, and a last relaxation to the full tolerance at the end), micro_replicas (1, the default: one environment; K: K replicas of the environment, each relaxed from its own environment of the core before, combined into the soft minimum -kT ln sum_k exp(-E_k / kT) of their surfaces, whose gradient is the weighted mean of theirs; not a free energy, at most kT ln K below the lowest replica; the files hold the lowest replica and NAME_replicas.xyz all of them), micro_replica_temperature (K of the soft minimum, 298.15 by default), micro_replica_start (perturb, the default: every free atom of the first relaxed environment moved by micro_replica_amplitude, 0.05 Angstrom, in a random direction of seed micro_replica_seed, 1; md: after micro_replica_md_steps, 200, steps of molecular dynamics of the environment at the temperature with the core held; files: the environments of the last K whole structures of micro_replica_files, such as the NAME_replicas.xyz of a run with replicas), traj_high_only (on or off, default off: write only the real high-layer atoms to optimization, MD and mapper XYZ trajectories)

test the SCF solution for instabilities every N evaluations and go on from a stabler one where it is unstable, repeating the evaluation there (0, the default: never; programs with an SCF that can test it, such as PySCF; the others say so once)

with -stability: an instability towards another kind of wavefunction (restricted to unrestricted): report (the default: it is said, the kind is kept), switch (go on with the unrestricted kind for the rest of the run), off (not tested)

how many structures are calculated at the same time where a command has several that do not depend on each other (the images of a chain, the two structures of a search between two structures, the states of a function of several states): the threads of the command for the built-in calculators, copies in worker processes for the calculators of the Python side. -core stays the threads of one calculation (0: as many structures at a time as -core has threads for the built-in calculators, one for those of the Python side)

an excited state (-es N, the states of -mf) is the state that was number N at the first structure and is followed from structure to structure by the overlaps of its amplitudes, instead of the state number N in the order of the energies at every structure (calculators that hand out their states: the built-in GFN0-xTB and PySCF with a restricted reference; a state that is not found again with certainty is reported)

file with the Hessian the run starts from (Cartesian, Hartree/Bohr^2): a NumPy file, an ORCA .hess file, a Gaussian .fchk file or output, or numbers only (the square or its lower triangle); the first Hessian that is asked for is taken from it

xyz file of displacements (any length): a transition-state search (-order 1) takes the Hessian mode closest to it uphill and then tracks that mode by overlap, instead of the lowest mode (RS-I-RFO becomes its mode-following variant mf_rsirfo_*); for example the tangent of a chain at the image it starts from; Cartesian coordinates

coordinate system of the optimization: cart, ric, dic, tric (translation-rotation internal coordinates, delocalized), tric-p (their primitive set), tric-cart[:WEIGHT] (TRIC stacked with weighted Cartesian coordinates), spherical (every atom by r, theta, phi about the centroid), hyperspherical or polar (the whole structure by its distance from the centroid and 3N-1 angles; hyperspherical:FILE about the structure of FILE; for optimizations, not chains), auto (tric-cart, or cart for atom clusters, dense or periodic networks and very large systems), or a registered name. Calculators always receive Cartesian structures.

user-defined bias potentials as expressions of geometric variables in atomic units (energy in Hartree), e.g. '0.15*(dist(1,2)-1.5*ang)^2'; functions dist, angle, dihedral, oop, x, y, z with atoms or groups [1-3]; see the bias documentation

the spin state as the number of unpaired electrons 2S instead of -spin (2S + 1), as the 'spin' of PySCF, xTB's uhf, and several Rust engines count it; one value, or one per state. It sets the state only: an unrestricted reference for singlets is -u
program-specific calculator settings as key=value (Python literals), e.g. density_fit=True conv_tol=1e-10; for -os ase:module:Class they are constructor keywords

user-defined constraints as expressions in the -ubias language: 'EXPR' holds the starting value, 'EXPR = VALUE' a value (atomic units; 'ang', 'deg' convert), '; period = 2*pi' wraps angle-like functions, '; tolerance = 1e-8' holds a noisy function to that residual instead of 1e-10, e.g. 'dist(1,2) - dist(3,4)'; with -vc the functions of the cell as well, e.g. 'volume()', 'cell_a() = 10.5*ang', 'cell_a()/cell_b()'

groups of atoms (ex.) 1,2,3 4,5 whose distances to each other are held at their values in the input (MultiOptPy: 'set the gradient of internal coordinates between atoms to zero'): every distance of a group is a constraint as -pc bond is, taken out of the gradient and of the Hessian and restored after every step
CCQN reaction-coordinate axis from reactive bonds, as atom pairs (ex.) 1,2 3,4
CCQN axis toward the midpoint of the straight line to this product structure (xyz)
cosine of the CCQN cone half-angle (default: 0.1 for bonds, 0.5 for a product)
CCQN uphill step and initial saddle trust radius in Angstrom (default: 0.1)
vibrations at or below this wavenumber (cm^-1) are left out of the thermochemistry

treatment of the thermal energy of low frequencies apart from that of the entropy (-freq_corr): head-gordon, truhlar, or none; without it, the one that goes with -freq_corr (grimme: head-gordon, truhlar: truhlar)
cutoff (cm^-1) of the treatment of the thermal energy; without it, -freq_cutoff
concentration (mol/L) for the translational entropy of a solute instead of the pressure of the gas
scale factor of the vibrational frequencies in the thermochemistry
scale factor of the frequencies in the zero-point energy; without it, -freq_scale
imaginary frequencies up to this magnitude (cm^-1) enter the thermochemistry as real ones
moment of inertia that bounds the free rotor of -freq_corr grimme: global (1e-44 kg m^2) or molecule (the mean moment of the molecule)
distance (Bohr) within which atoms coincide in the point-group analysis
vibrational analysis: project the direction of the gradient out with the rigid-body motions (the modes orthogonal to a reaction path at a point that is not stationary)

after a converged optimization, the derivatives in every constant of the bias options (a force constant, an equilibrium value, the AFIR collision energy, ...; per unit of the option as it is written): of the bias energy, and how the stationary point and its energy without the bias move with the constant (dx/dp = -H^+ dg/dp with the Hessian of the whole surface); written to bias_derivatives.csv and the log

-mf opt_meci: do not check the branching plane with gradients at displaced structures when the search has converged (the check costs four evaluations of both states and sends the search on if the point is not stationary on the seam)

-mf opt_mesx, -mf opt_meci: what a step is judged by when the trust radius is adapted: energy (the change of the mean energy of the two states against the quadratic model of the projected gradient, as for a search on one surface) or merit (the change of the function the projected gradient belongs to: the mean energy within the seam and (E1 - E2)^2 / |g1 - g2|)

optimize the cell together with the atoms (cells periodic in three directions; the stress comes from the calculator, or from differences of the energy where it has none); with -es the stress of that state, with -mf the two states combined in the variables of the cell (their enthalpies and their gradients in the variables: crossing points and conical intersections with the cell)
-vc: external pressure in GPa; the enthalpy E + P V is minimized

-vc: artificial force on the cell (periodic AFIR): pairs of a collision energy in kJ/mol (positive: compress, negative: expand; a ramp as for -ma) and the distances it acts on, a list of a, b, c (origin to the tip of a lattice vector) and ab, bc, ca (between two tips), e.g. -vc_afir 200 a,b -vc_afir -100 ab

-vc: hard constraints on the cell, comma-separated, at the values of the input or NAME=VALUE: a, b, c (lengths, Angstrom), alpha, beta, gamma (degrees), volume (Angstrom^3; only the shape relaxes), shape (b/a, c/a and the three angles; only an isotropic scaling relaxes), a_vector, b_vector, c_vector (the three Cartesian components of a lattice vector, e.g. the normal vector of a slab), ax, ay, ..., cz (one component, Angstrom); the same constraints as -uc 'cell_a()', 'volume()', ...; e.g. -vc_fix volume, -vc_fix c_vector, -vc_fix a=10.5,gamma

-irc: further settings of the IRC as KEY=VALUE: first_step (check, the default: test the first point of each side and replace it by the energy minimum on a hypersphere around the transition state when it fails; off: MultiOptPy's first point), angle (largest angle in degrees between the downhill direction at the first point and the transition vector, 10), rho_min and rho_max (limits of actual over predicted energy change of the first step, 0.75 and 1.25), initial (mass-weighted length of the displacement from the transition state, 0.1 of the step size), sides (both, forward, backward), masses (standard: atomic weights, as the vibrational analysis; isotope: the most abundant isotopes, as MultiOptPy), energy_rise (retry, the default: a step that raised the energy is taken again at half its length, LQA and Euler; stop: end a side where the energy rises; off: keep such points, as MultiOptPy), overshoot (retry, the default, with energy_rise=retry: a step whose end has a gradient that points back along it is taken again at half its length; keep: such points stay), bend (off, the default; a share such as 0.25: no step is longer than the one that loses this share of the energy it gains by cutting the bend of the valley, from the curvature of the path and the Hessian across it; for exact Hessians along the path, -fc 1), approach (on, the default: below the force thresholds a side goes on to the minimum until the gradient is below approach_max_force and approach_rms_force, LQA, Euler, RK4; off: end at the first point below the thresholds, as MultiOptPy), approach_max_force (0.000015), approach_rms_force (0.00001), approach_steps (100), max_force (0.0004), rms_force (0.0001), min_points (10), oscillations (5), sphere_iterations (30), sphere_gradient (1e-4), sphere_step (1e-3)

-mf bitss REFERENCE: settings of the binary-image transition state search as KEY=VALUE: f (reduction of the separation per stage, 0.5), alpha (10), beta (0.1), interval (iterations between two settings of the coefficients, 100), points (points between the images for the barrier estimate, 3), min_separation (Bohr, 0.01), stages (30), step_share (longest step as a share of the separation asked for, 0.5; none: no limit), midpoint_shift (end when the midpoint moved by less than this share of the reduction of a stage; none), midpoint_gradient (true)
-vc: weight w of the lattice variables, gamma = w sqrt(number of atoms) (Gubler et al. 2023; values between 1 and 2 are recommended there)
show on the screen what the optimization methods do inside a step (the messages of the inner solvers, such as those of RS-I-RFO); they are always written to mopt.log
at convergence, check the Hessian and leave a stationary point that has more negative curvatures than -order asks for (0: a minimum), then go on; needs Hessians from the calculator
solver of the CCQN uphill subproblem: exact (global) or alm (the paper's method)

user-defined bias potentials as expressions of geometric variables in atomic units (energy in Hartree), e.g. '0.15*(dist(1,2)-1.5*ang)^2'; functions dist, angle, dihedral, oop, x, y, z with atoms or groups [1-3]; see the bias documentation (shared by every step: merged into every step block of the settings file, where a step that sets it itself wins; also the block shared_settings of the settings file)

user-defined constraints as expressions in the -ubias language: 'EXPR' holds the starting value, 'EXPR = VALUE' a value (atomic units; 'ang', 'deg' convert), '; period = 2*pi' wraps angle-like functions, '; tolerance = 1e-8' holds a noisy function to that residual instead of 1e-10, e.g. 'dist(1,2) - dist(3,4)'; with -vc the functions of the cell as well, e.g. 'volume()', 'cell_a() = 10.5*ang', 'cell_a()/cell_b()' (shared by every step: merged into every step block of the settings file, where a step that sets it itself wins; also the block shared_settings of the settings file)

groups of atoms (ex.) 1,2,3 4,5 whose distances to each other are held at their values in the input (MultiOptPy: 'set the gradient of internal coordinates between atoms to zero'): every distance of a group is a constraint as -pc bond is, taken out of the gradient and of the Hessian and restored after every step (shared by every step: merged into every step block of the settings file, where a step that sets it itself wins; also the block shared_settings of the settings file)

-vc: hard constraints on the cell, comma-separated, at the values of the input or NAME=VALUE: a, b, c (lengths, Angstrom), alpha, beta, gamma (degrees), volume (Angstrom^3; only the shape relaxes), shape (b/a, c/a and the three angles; only an isotropic scaling relaxes), a_vector, b_vector, c_vector (the three Cartesian components of a lattice vector, e.g. the normal vector of a slab), ax, ay, ..., cz (one component, Angstrom); the same constraints as -uc 'cell_a()', 'volume()', ...; e.g. -vc_fix volume, -vc_fix c_vector, -vc_fix a=10.5,gamma (shared by every step: merged into every step block of the settings file, where a step that sets it itself wins; also the block shared_settings of the settings file)

options.help: Path to the JSON configuration file. Default: ./config.json
Path to software_path.conf. Default: ./software_path.conf
Seed AFIR parameters for Step 1 (overrides step1_settings in config). Format: gamma_kJmol frag1_atoms frag2_atoms ... Example: -ma 100.0 1,2 3,4,5
Number of NEB candidates to refine. Overrides config.
Boltzmann temperature [K]. Default: from mapper_settings or 300.
RMSD threshold for structure identity [A]. Default: 0.30.
Maximum number of AutoTSWorkflow invocations (0=unlimited). Default: 50.
Auto-generated AFIR gamma [kJ/mol]. Default: 100.0.
Max AFIR atom-pair perturbations per node. Default: 9999.
AFIR distance window lower bound [A]. Default: 1.5.
AFIR distance window upper bound [A]. Default: 5.0.
Root directory for all mapper outputs. Default: mapper_output.
Random seed for reproducibility. Default: 42.
1-based atom label numbers to restrict AFIR pair search. Only pairs formed between these atoms will be generated. Example: --active_atoms 1 2 5 6  Default: all atoms are considered.
Also generate repulsive (negative gamma) AFIR perturbations for every selected atom pair, in addition to the default attractive (positive gamma) direction.

EQ node IDs to exclude from AFIR exploration.  Matching nodes are still registered in the reaction network graph but will never be used as starting points for new AFIR runs.  Example: --exclude_nodes 3 7 12  Default: no exclusions.

Automatically exclude any newly found EQ node whose covalent bond topology differs from that of the seed structure (EQ0).  Useful for restricting exploration to a single potential-energy surface without crossing into reactive products.  Default: disabled.

Use the RCMC (Rate Constant Matrix Contraction) algorithm to determine exploration priorities instead of the default Boltzmann queue.  Requires --rcmc_temperature and optionally --rcmc_time.  Default: disabled.
Temperature [K] for the RCMC priority calculation.  Only used when --use_rcmc is set.  Default: from mapper_settings or 300.
Reaction time [s] for the RCMC priority calculation.  Only used when --use_rcmc is set.  Default: from mapper_settings or 1.0.

EQ node ID to use as the initial population source in the RCMC kinetic simulation.  The transient population vector is initialised with p[start_node]=1 before contraction.  Only used when --use_rcmc is set.  Default: from mapper_settings["rcmc_start_node_id"] or 0 (EQ0).
Resume from an existing reaction_network.json.

Each task is executed in its own spawned subprocess so that os.chdir() calls inside AutoTSWorkflow are fully isolated.  1 (default) gives sequential execution identical to the single-process behaviour.  Overrides mapper_settings.n_parallel.
Logging verbosity. Default: INFO.
