options.help: further settings of the mapper as KEY=VALUE (the same keys may stand in mapper_settings of the settings file): method (the way a minimum is explored: afir_ts, the default, AFIR pushes between pairs of atoms; addf, the anharmonic downward distortion following from the minimum; nanoreactor, molecular dynamics in the nanoreactor walls and a two-point method between the minima of every reaction it shows; connect, the missing connections between the starts and the goal: the gaps of the path of least weight D^2 between the known minima, each filled by a two-point method; or a registered one), priority (the choice of the next minimum: boltzmann, the default, at temperature_K; tabu, water_filling, water_filling_adaptive, boltzmann_heated, tabu_heated; rrt, the default with goal, towards the goal: fair random choices among the groups of minima of one connection pattern alternating with choices by the similarity of the local atomic environments to the goal; or a registered one), goal (FILE: the goal structure, the first frame of an xyz file or a variables file, optimized like the inputs and never explored), goal_stop (true, the default: the exploration ends when the goal is joined to a start; false), goal_match (structure, the default: the goal structure itself; bonds: any minimum with its bond graph), accept_temperature (K: a new minimum is explored only with the probability min(1, exp(-(E_PT - E_X) / kT)), E_PT the highest transition state on the way of its job from the minimum X; 7500 by default with priority=rrt, off otherwise), rrt_goal_weight (c of the choices by similarity, 1), rrt_locality (per Angstrom, 20), higher_saddles (false, the default: saddle points of order 2 or more that a search or an IRC meets are kept as nodes 2SP, 3SP, ... without following their links, and a search that ends at one goes on by mode kill to a transition state; true: they are optimized at their order and descended from along each unstable mode; experimental), max_saddle_order (2), upward (false; true: upward searches by high-index saddle dynamics from the transition states of every minimum to saddle points of order 2), upward_modes (2), confirm_bifurcations (false; true: a possible bifurcation of an IRC is tried both ways across the path and minimized), irc_hessian_interval (10: the points between the exact Hessians that the IRC computes on its own where the Hessian is analytic, irc_hessians; the lowest curvature across the path at each of them is kept, and a possible bifurcation says at which arc length that curvature changes sign), confirm_dissociations (false; true: a relaxed scan of the distance between the two molecules of every complex towards its dissociation channel, in steps of dissociation_scan_step, 0.3 Angstrom; a maximum more than dissociation_scan_tolerance, 0.5 kcal/mol, above the channel is a barrier), path_peaks (failed, the default: the highest point of a path that gave no transition state is saved with the minima on its two sides, as a record beside the network; all: that of every path; off), ts_conformers (false; true: the conformers of every transition state are searched with its saddle direction held, the search of confsearch -tsconf with the settings of the block ts_conformer_settings of the settings file, and every saddle point found is followed like any guess), entrance_structures (0; N: the molecules of the first input are an entrance channel, and N structures of it, the molecules turned and placed in contact at random, are further inputs of the run), entrance_contact (1.0: the nearest atoms of two molecules at this times the sum of their van der Waals radii), max_bond_changes and max_species_changes (no limit by default; N: a new minimum is not explored when its bonds, or its chemical species by the SMILES string, changed more than N times on the way from its input; 0: only what keeps the bonds, or the species, of the inputs is explored), method_step1 (afir_ts: the method of the first path of a pair of atoms; afir, the default, the AFIR push; se_gsm, the single-ended growing string driven by the pair, or gnt, the Newton trajectory that shortens it, grown from the minimum without a push; method_step1_KEY its settings; neb and dmf are methods of method_relax, and a method of two ends runs with method=connect and a goal), stop (further stop rules, ';' between them: nothing_new:N, rank_unchanged:R,N, max_jobs:N), store (further stores of the network, ',' between them, besides the files of the run directory: sqlite, the network as the SQLite database reaction_network.sqlite, or a registered one), save_job_steps (true by default: save stage trajectories, each NEB iteration and live job progress), html_report (true, the default; false), mirror (false, the default: mirror images are different minima; true), verify_minima (true, the default: every minimum is verified by its Hessian, mode kill is opt-in, and its wavenumbers are kept; false: converged structures are taken unchecked), irc_hessians (true, the default: the IRC computes the exact Hessian at every tenth point unless calc_exact_hess of step4_settings says otherwise, and a negative curvature across the path there is recorded as a possible bifurcation; false: only where calc_exact_hess asks), irc_end_threshold_cm1 (minimum magnitude of an imaginary vibration at an optimized IRC endpoint for a TS–TS link, cm^-1, 50), bifurcation_threshold_cm1 (how negative that curvature must be, cm^-1, 50), variable_tolerance (on an objective of plain variables, othersoft mb2d and the like: the largest distance of two points that are the same, in the units of the variables, 0.01; the method is then addf by default), channels (true, the default: an end of an IRC whose molecules are apart is a dissociation channel DC, its fragments optimized on their own once, and a minimum of two molecules in contact dissociates into its channel without a barrier; false: none), channel_margin (Angstrom over the sums of the van der Waals radii for molecules in contact, 1.0), method_KEY (a setting of the method: for afir_ts relax (neb, the default: the AFIR path is relaxed without the force by the chain relaxation of nebmain, with Hessian-based steps from a model Hessian and step2_settings as its settings, and the guesses are the maxima of the relaxed chain; dmf; off: the maxima of the AFIR path itself) and relax_KEY (a setting of that method); for addf the keys of addf of the two-point methods, such as method_paths=8, and dissociation (bond scale of the test for a dissociation channel, 2.0) and dissociation_atoms; for connect path (the two-point method of a gap, neb), path_KEY, and attempts (attempts of one pair, 2; attempt k runs with 2^(k-1) times the images); for nanoreactor runs, steps, time_step, temperature, frame_every, r1, r2, k1, k2, period, wide, detect, persist, quench_every, events, path (neb), path_KEY, segment (on: the frames around a reaction are the first path), and segment_frames; see mapper.md), workers (jobs at the same time, 1 by default; --max_workers and MultiOptPy's n_parallel set it too), batch_size (jobs chosen together, the number of workers by default: the network depends on it and not on the number of workers), schedule (batch, the default: the jobs of a batch are kept in the order of their numbers when all have ended; rolling: a job starts whenever a worker is free and is kept when it ends, so that the network can depend on the timing); kinetics (off, the default; on: when the exploration ends, not when it is interrupted, the kinetics of the network runs with the kinetics_* settings below, its files in kinetics/ of the run directory and a section in the report); with priority=kinetics (the kinetic priority, which --use_rcmc selects) and with kinetics=on: kinetics_score (population, the default as MultiOptPy; max_population, residence, discovery_flux), kinetics_solver (propagate, the default; rcmc, legacy_rcmc for MultiOptPy's numbers, expm), kinetics_time (s, 1.0; --rcmc_time), kinetics_temperature (K, the temperature of the run; --rcmc_temperature), kinetics_start (node of the start population, the first input; --rcmc_start_node), kinetics_energy (electronic, the default; free), kinetics_clamp (consistent, legacy, none), kinetics_time_rule (gershgorin, eigen, diag), kinetics_tolerance (of propagate, 1e-8), kinetics_rate_theory (eyring, tst), kinetics_corrections (',' between them: wigner, bell, eckart, skodje_truhlar, kappa, landau_zener, zhu_nakamura), kinetics_kappa; states (the electronic states of the run, PES1, PES2, ...: CHARGE,MULTIPLICITY or CHARGE,MULTIPLICITY,ROOT with ';' between them, e.g. states=0,1;0,3: every minimum lies on its state, and its crossing tasks find the minimum-energy crossing points with every other state, MECP between spin states, MECI between two roots of one spin: an AFIR path gives candidates, each is optimized by the gradient projection without the force, and a meta-IRC runs down from the crossing point on both states), crossings (true, the default with states; false: each surface on its own), crossing_pairs (all, the default: every pair of states; adjacent: PESk with PESk-1 and PESk+1 only), crossing_afir (the AFIR paths, for every push of afir_ts: gp, the default, the force on the gradient projection, whose end and the minima of the seam model function along it are the candidates; model, on the seam model function, MECP, or the Avoiding model function, MECI, whose end and minima along the path are the candidates; both; off), crossing_direct (false; true: also from the minimum itself), crossing_pushes (the AFIR pushes of the paths by their fragments, GAMMA:ATOMS:ATOMS with ';' between them, instead of the pairs of atoms of afir_ts), crossing_from (all, the default; inputs: crossing tasks from the inputs alone), ts_states (none, or the states, PES numbers with ',' between them, on which transition states are searched; all by default), crossing_smf_alpha (Hartree, 30 kJ/mol), crossing_amf_alpha (Hartree, 30 kJ/mol), crossing_amf_branch (upper, lower), crossing_candidate_prominence (Hartree, 0.5 kJ/mol: how far the function along an AFIR path must rise on both sides of a minimum for it to be a candidate; 0: every minimum), crossing_candidate_distance (Angstrom, 0.05: the smallest root-mean-square displacement between two candidates of a path and between a candidate and a crossing point the job has found; 0: none), crossing_parallel_stop (off, the default; on: a crossing search is ended where its two states run parallel, the gap at most crossing_gap and the difference of the two gradients below crossing_parallel_gradient, 0.01 Hartree/Bohr, for crossing_parallel_steps, 10, iterations in a row), crossing_step (Angstrom, 0.1), crossing_gap (Hartree, 1e-3: the largest gap of the two states at the end of a converged crossing search; with a larger one the end is no crossing point, a warning says so, and no meta-IRC runs from it), crossing_seam_check (on, the default: every accepted crossing point is analysed within the seam with the Hessians of both states, and one with an imaginary mode there is kept as a saddle point on the seam, not a minimum-energy crossing point; off: not checked); the network of a run on another surface: -remap

settings of the HTML report (mapper_report.html, written after jobs) as KEY=VALUE: unit (kcal, the default; kj, ev, hartree), temperature (298.15: K of the Boltzmann populations of the minima), energy_window (none, the default: every node; a number: only the nodes at most this far above the lowest minimum, in the unit), max_minima (all, the default; N: the lowest N minima shown, with the links between them), structures (400: the most nodes whose structure is in the page, the lowest first, for its viewer and downloads), structure_atoms (100000: the most atoms of those structures together), irc_lines (60000: the most atom lines of the IRC paths in the page, the lowest transition states first, at most 30 frames each), structure_packed_atoms and irc_packed_lines (every one, the default: the structures and paths beyond those are in the page packed, unpacked by the browser when one is shown or saved; a number limits them, 0: none), figure_minima (300: the minima of the disconnectivity graph and the energy diagram, and of the figures drawn without scripts), table_rows (300: rows of each table without scripts), profile_points (100000: points of the IRC energies in the page), map_exact (1000: up to this many structures the map is classical scaling of all distances, above it landmark scaling), map_landmarks (400), file (mapper_report.html: the name of the page in the run directory)

write the HTML report of the run directory RUN_DIR again from its files (a run that ended, was stopped, or is still running), or from the database of a run (reaction_network.sqlite of store=sqlite, the page written next to it), with the settings of the page of the run and those of -report_opt; no input is needed and nothing is computed; what the files lack is listed on the page instead of stopping it

draw the network of the run directory RUN_DIR (or of the database of a run) again on the surface of this run (-cfg, -map_opt), in a run directory of its own (--output_dir): its minima are the inputs (no input file is given), each minimized on its state, and every transition state, crossing point (MECP, MECI) and saddle point of higher order of it is one job: for a transition state the minima of its ends and the structures of its path file as the first chain of method_path (neb; method_path_KEY its settings; method_path=none: its transition state is the guess), the maxima followed to transition states and their IRCs; for a crossing point the refinement on the gradient projection of its two states and the meta-IRC on each; for a saddle point its optimization at its order and its descents (higher_saddles=on). The first run is only read; a network of several states needs the same number of states (states); without a limit of jobs given every item runs; remap.csv of the run directory says what each minimum and item became

the energies of every node of the network of the run directory RUN_DIR (or of the database of a run) on the surface of this run (-cfg, -map_opt), at the structures of that network, in a run directory of its own (--output_dir): no input file, no optimization and no Hessian. A minimum, a transition state and a saddle point of higher order have one energy on their state, a crossing point (MECP, MECI) the energies of its two states (the node has their mean, single_points.csv their gap), a dissociation channel the sum of its fragments. The network of the run is the first one with these energies (the same nodes, labels and frequencies, the barriers computed again; free energies shifted by the change of the energy); its report and kinetics (kinetics=on) are those of any run. --max_workers energies at a time; a stopped run continues with --restart; the first run is only read

the networks of the run directories RUN_DIR ... (or the databases of runs) written as one network in a run directory of its own (--output_dir), without a calculation and without an input file: the first as it is, the nodes of the others added where the merged network has no node that is the same (rmsd_threshold, energy_tolerance_kcalmol, mirror), their edges where it has none with the same transition state, crossing point or saddle point, their jobs and inputs appended. The runs must have the same atoms in the same order and the same states; that they ran on the same surface is the word of the user. merge.csv says what every node of every run is in the merged network; the directory is read by run_kinetics, -remap and -single_points and is not continued by --restart

Energy type used for rate-constant calculations.             'electronic' (default) uses the SCF energy (energy_hartree).             'free' uses the Gibbs free energy (free_energy_hartree).             In free mode, nodes whose free_energy_hartree is null are             removed along with all edges connected to them before RCMC.
Logging verbosity (default: WARNING).

the frames of INPUT are the points of a reaction path (in a common orientation): the vibrations orthogonal to the path at every point and where the lowest turns unstable (valley-ridge transitions, at which a path bifurcates), the curvature of the path and its couplings to the modes (reaction-path Hamiltonian), their components along internal coordinates and the reaction phases (unified reaction valley approach), the free-energy profile with the variational transition state at -temp, and tunneling (ZCT, SCT)
START,END,STEP (K): the thermodynamic functions at these temperatures as well, in thermochemistry_scan.csv
electronic energies (Hartree) from another level of theory, one per input, that replace those of the calculator in the thermochemistry
with several inputs: their relative Gibbs free energies and Boltzmann populations at -temp, in boltzmann_<time>.csv

anharmonic analysis of a minimum: cubic and quartic force constants from the Hessians at structures displaced along every normal mode (two per vibration), fundamentals and zero-point energy by second-order perturbation theory (VPT2) and by the vibrational self-consistent field (VSCF)
-anharmonic: displacement along every normal mode in its dimensionless normal coordinate
-anharmonic: harmonic oscillator functions per mode in VSCF
-anharmonic: largest frequency gap (cm^-1) of a Fermi resonance
-anharmonic: a term is a Fermi resonance when its correction beyond perturbation theory exceeds this (cm^-1)

N1 N2 N3: phonons of a periodic structure from the force constants of the supercell of N1 x N2 x N3 cells (its Hessian is computed); with -phonon_path the dispersion, with -phonon_mesh the density of states and the thermodynamic functions of the crystal
wave vectors in units of the reciprocal lattice vectors, e.g. 0,0,0 0.5,0,0 0.5,0.5,0: the phonon dispersion along the lines between them (phonon_dispersion.csv)
-phonon_path: steps along every line
M1 M2 M3: mesh of wave vectors for the density of states (phonon_dos.csv) and the thermodynamic functions per cell (phonon_thermochemistry.txt)
-phonon_mesh: width (cm^-1) of the Gaussian of every mode in the density of states

local vibrational modes (Konkoli-Cremer) of internal coordinates: the relaxed force constant and the frequency of each coordinate decoupled from the rest. Coordinates by atom numbers starting at 1: 1-2 (distance), 1-2-3 (angle), 1-2-3-4 (dihedral); bonds (all bonds), auto (all bonds, angles, and dihedrals)
also analyse the vibrations of these atoms alone (numbers starting at 1, e.g. 1,4,7-9) from their part of the Hessian; see -partial_hessian

-partial_atoms: block (the block of the chosen atoms, their translations and rotations projected out), effective (the other atoms relaxed: the Schur complement, then the same projection; for two atoms the relaxed force constant of the local stretching mode), or frozen (the block in the fixed frame of the other atoms, no projection)
-partial_hessian effective: besides their free rotations about the chosen atoms, directions of the other atoms whose curvature is below this fraction of their largest one are left out (exact zeros)

-path: direction of the path at its points: gradient (a steepest-descent path such as an intrinsic reaction coordinate; the points are used where the gradient vanishes) or points (the line through the neighbouring points, for a scan or a band of images)

masses of the normal modes, the thermochemistry and -path: standard (the standard atomic weights) or isotope (the most abundant isotopes, as the IRC option masses=isotope and MultiOptPy); named in thermochemistry.txt and the log. Not available with -anharmonic, -local_modes, -partial_atoms, -phonon_supercell and -mf, which weight with the standard atomic weights

natural reaction orbitals along the frames of the input (a path): at every frame the pairs of an occupied and an empty orbital through which the electrons respond to the displacement along the path, and their singular values (Ebisawa et al., Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2022, 24, 3532); needs a calculator that hands out orbitals (gfn0xtb, gfn1xtb, pyscf, tblite)
orbital energies along the frames of the input (a path), each orbital followed from frame to frame, their derivatives, and the orbitals whose energies change most (reactive orbital energy theory)

N M ...: two or more excited states (numbers at the first frame, 1: the lowest) along the frames of the input (a path) as diabatic states: the diabatic potential matrix (their energies and couplings), where two of them cross, and the Landau-Zener probability of a passage at -temp, from the overlaps of the states of neighbouring frames (propagative block-diagonalisation diabatisation); for calculators that hand out their excited states (gfn0xtb, pyscf)
-nro: displacement along the path for the differences of the orbitals, in amu^0.5 Bohr
-path: a minimum of the path curvature divides two reaction phases when the curvature rises on both sides by more than this fraction of its largest value (0: every minimum)

a middle layer of -oniom: ATOMS LINK CALCULATOR (as -oniom; ATOMS hold the atoms of the high layer and more): three-layer ONIOM, E_low(real) + E_middle(middle) - E_low(middle) + E_high(model) - E_middle(model)

settings of -oniom as KEY=VALUE: low.KEY=VALUE and middle.KEY=VALUE (settings of the calculator of that level, which can be any calculator of -os, an ASE calculator among them: method, basis, and its own keys as -calc_opt takes them; -func, -bs, and -calc_opt belong to the highest level and are not handed down), link (scaled, the default: the link atom at the share g = (R(Q1) + R(H)) / (R(Q1) + R(Q2)) of the bond, as Gaussian; distance: at R(Q1) + R(H) from Q1, as MultiOptPy), high_charge and high_multiplicity, middle_charge and middle_multiplicity (the model systems; by default the charge of the whole structure and its multiplicity, changed by one where the link atoms change the parity of the electrons), embedding (mechanical, the default; electronic: the higher level of every region in the charges of the atoms around it, the Coulomb energy of the model with them taken off with the lower level), charges (lowest, the default: the lowest level's, the topology charges of GFN-FF; or FILE: one per atom, in e), boundary (rc, the default: the charge of each Q2 moved to the midpoints of its bonds to the environment; zero; keep), micro (on by default: optmain, ircmain, and the chains of nebmain move the core, the outermost model region and the outer atoms of its links, and relax the rest on the lowest level (with electronic embedding the whole surface) to a minimum before every evaluation; Hessians are those of the core; the files hold the whole system; off: every atom moves), micro_mode_kill (off, the default: the environment, the low layer, is not mode-killed, the core is by its optimizer; N: the check for negative curvature of the environment after the first and every Nth relaxation, its modes followed down), micro_curvature (guided, the default: the check starts from the softest mode of the last one and takes the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxation as preconditioner; plain: from a fixed start without one), micro_precondition (lindh2007d3, the default, or another model Hessian of -modelhess, or none: its block of the environment, built at the free atoms and the fixed atoms within 4 Angstrom of the environment and shifted by micro_precondition_shift, default 1e-3 Hartree/Bohr^2, is the initial matrix of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations and the preconditioner of the curvature check; up to 16 are kept, one per structure they were built near; environments of at most 6000 variables; a relaxation that fails with it is made again without it), micro_tolerance (largest gradient component of the relaxed environment; by default micro_tolerance_factor times the thresholds of the forces of the run itself, the largest force and the RMS force of its criteria; a relaxation whose line search fails goes on with FIRE, one that ends above its tolerance says so), micro_tolerance_factor (1, the default, or a smaller share such as 0.1 of the thresholds of the forces of the run to which the environment is relaxed, not below 1e-5; up to 1), micro_check_tolerance (largest gradient component of the environment, Hartree/Bohr, for every Hessian of a check of stability: the verification of a converged saddle-point search, the start of an IRC, the stationary points of the mapper, a vibrational analysis; 1e-5 by default, never looser than the relaxations of the run; an environment that stands on a saddle point of its own is moved off it and relaxed again before any Hessian, and the error of the curvatures of a check is estimated by moving the environment to the minimum of its quadratic model and taking the Hessian again), micro_correct (on, the default, or off: correct the energy and the core gradient for the gradient left in the environment by the response of the newest Hessian of the core, where that moves the environment by at most 0.05 Bohr), micro_core_shell (Angstrom: the free atoms of the environment within that distance of the model region are moved by the optimizer with the core; by default none), micro_hessian (effective, the default: the Hessian of the relaxed surface; approximate: the same with the inverse of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations; held: the core block with the environment held), micro_hessian_solve (auto, the default: the response of the environment from its dense block, by the analytic Hessian of the lowest level or central differences of its gradient, where that costs fewer gradients than conjugate gradients and fits in the memory, conjugate gradients otherwise; dense; cg), micro_hessian_memory (GiB the Hessian of the core may take, by default half of the free memory: the analytic Hessian of the whole system where its matrices fit, central differences otherwise, refused where those do not fit either), micro_hessian_shell (Angstrom: only the environment within that distance of the core responds in the Hessian of the core, the rest is held; by default all of it), micro_optimizer (lbfgs, the default; tn: truncated Newton; or a method of -opt, for environments of at most 500 atoms), micro_coord (cart, the default; fragments: translation, rotation, and internal coordinates of each fragment of the environment), micro_predict (on or off, the default: start each relaxation from the predicted response of the environment), micro_adaptive (0, the default; ETA: the tolerance of a relaxation ETA times the largest core gradient while that is large, and a last relaxation to the full tolerance at the end), micro_replicas (1, the default: one environment; K: K replicas of the environment, each relaxed from its own environment of the core before, combined into the soft minimum -kT ln sum_k exp(-E_k / kT) of their surfaces, whose gradient is the weighted mean of theirs; not a free energy, at most kT ln K below the lowest replica; the files hold the lowest replica and NAME_replicas.xyz all of them), micro_replica_temperature (K of the soft minimum, 298.15 by default), micro_replica_start (perturb, the default: every free atom of the first relaxed environment moved by micro_replica_amplitude, 0.05 Angstrom, in a random direction of seed micro_replica_seed, 1; md: after micro_replica_md_steps, 200, steps of molecular dynamics of the environment at the temperature with the core held; files: the environments of the last K whole structures of micro_replica_files, such as the NAME_replicas.xyz of a run with replicas), traj_high_only (on or off, default off: write only the real high-layer atoms to optimization, MD and mapper XYZ trajectories)

test the SCF solution for instabilities every N evaluations and go on from a stabler one where it is unstable, repeating the evaluation there (0, the default: never; programs with an SCF that can test it, such as PySCF; the others say so once)

with -stability: an instability towards another kind of wavefunction (restricted to unrestricted): report (the default: it is said, the kind is kept), switch (go on with the unrestricted kind for the rest of the run), off (not tested)

how many structures are calculated at the same time where a command has several that do not depend on each other (the images of a chain, the two structures of a search between two structures, the states of a function of several states): the threads of the command for the built-in calculators, copies in worker processes for the calculators of the Python side. -core stays the threads of one calculation (0: as many structures at a time as -core has threads for the built-in calculators, one for those of the Python side)

an excited state (-es N, the states of -mf) is the state that was number N at the first structure and is followed from structure to structure by the overlaps of its amplitudes, instead of the state number N in the order of the energies at every structure (calculators that hand out their states: the built-in GFN0-xTB and PySCF with a restricted reference; a state that is not found again with certainty is reported)

file with the Hessian the run starts from (Cartesian, Hartree/Bohr^2): a NumPy file, an ORCA .hess file, a Gaussian .fchk file or output, or numbers only (the square or its lower triangle); the first Hessian that is asked for is taken from it

xyz file of displacements (any length): a transition-state search (-order 1) takes the Hessian mode closest to it uphill and then tracks that mode by overlap, instead of the lowest mode (RS-I-RFO becomes its mode-following variant mf_rsirfo_*); for example the tangent of a chain at the image it starts from; Cartesian coordinates

N: the check for negative curvature of the environment after the first and every Nth relaxation, its modes followed down), micro_curvature (guided, the default: the check starts from the softest mode of the last one and takes the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxation as preconditioner; plain: from a fixed start without one), micro_precondition (lindh2007d3, the default, or another model Hessian of -modelhess, or none: its block of the environment, built at the free atoms and the fixed atoms within 4 Angstrom of the environment and shifted by micro_precondition_shift, default 1e-3 Hartree/Bohr^2, is the initial matrix of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations and the preconditioner of the curvature check; up to 16 are kept, one per structure they were built near; environments of at most 6000 variables; a relaxation that fails with it is made again without it), micro_tolerance (largest gradient component of the relaxed environment; by default micro_tolerance_factor times the thresholds of the forces of the run itself, the largest force and the RMS force of its criteria; a relaxation whose line search fails goes on with FIRE, one that ends above its tolerance says so), micro_tolerance_factor (1, the default, or a smaller share such as 0.1 of the thresholds of the forces of the run to which the environment is relaxed, not below 1e-5; up to 1), micro_check_tolerance (largest gradient component of the environment, Hartree/Bohr, for every Hessian of a check of stability: the verification of a converged saddle-point search, the start of an IRC, the stationary points of the mapper, a vibrational analysis; 1e-5 by default, never looser than the relaxations of the run; an environment that stands on a saddle point of its own is moved off it and relaxed again before any Hessian, and the error of the curvatures of a check is estimated by moving the environment to the minimum of its quadratic model and taking the Hessian again), micro_correct (on, the default, or off: correct the energy and the core gradient for the gradient left in the environment by the response of the newest Hessian of the core, where that moves the environment by at most 0.05 Bohr), micro_core_shell (Angstrom: the free atoms of the environment within that distance of the model region are moved by the optimizer with the core; by default none), micro_hessian (effective, the default: the Hessian of the relaxed surface; approximate: the same with the inverse of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations; held: the core block with the environment held), micro_hessian_solve (auto, the default: the response of the environment from its dense block, by the analytic Hessian of the lowest level or central differences of its gradient, where that costs fewer gradients than conjugate gradients and fits in the memory, conjugate gradients otherwise; dense; cg), micro_hessian_memory (GiB the Hessian of the core may take, by default half of the free memory: the analytic Hessian of the whole system where its matrices fit, central differences otherwise, refused where those do not fit either), micro_hessian_shell (Angstrom: only the environment within that distance of the core responds in the Hessian of the core, the rest is held; by default all of it), micro_optimizer (lbfgs, the default; tn: truncated Newton; or a method of -opt, for environments of at most 500 atoms), micro_coord (cart, the default; fragments: translation, rotation, and internal coordinates of each fragment of the environment), micro_predict (on or off, the default: start each relaxation from the predicted response of the environment), micro_adaptive (0, the default; ETA: the tolerance of a relaxation ETA times the largest core gradient while that is large, and a last relaxation to the full tolerance at the end), micro_replicas (1, the default: one environment; K: K replicas of the environment, each relaxed from its own environment of the core before, combined into the soft minimum -kT ln sum_k exp(-E_k / kT) of their surfaces, whose gradient is the weighted mean of theirs; not a free energy, at most kT ln K below the lowest replica; the files hold the lowest replica and NAME_replicas.xyz all of them), micro_replica_temperature (K of the soft minimum, 298.15 by default), micro_replica_start (perturb, the default: every free atom of the first relaxed environment moved by micro_replica_amplitude, 0.05 Angstrom, in a random direction of seed micro_replica_seed, 1; md: after micro_replica_md_steps, 200, steps of molecular dynamics of the environment at the temperature with the core held; files: the environments of the last K whole structures of micro_replica_files, such as the NAME_replicas.xyz of a run with replicas), traj_high_only (on or off, default off: write only the real high-layer atoms to optimization, MD and mapper XYZ trajectories)

test the SCF solution for instabilities every N evaluations and go on from a stabler one where it is unstable, repeating the evaluation there (0, the default: never; programs with an SCF that can test it, such as PySCF; the others say so once)

with -stability: an instability towards another kind of wavefunction (restricted to unrestricted): report (the default: it is said, the kind is kept), switch (go on with the unrestricted kind for the rest of the run), off (not tested)

how many structures are calculated at the same time where a command has several that do not depend on each other (the images of a chain, the two structures of a search between two structures, the states of a function of several states): the threads of the command for the built-in calculators, copies in worker processes for the calculators of the Python side. -core stays the threads of one calculation (0: as many structures at a time as -core has threads for the built-in calculators, one for those of the Python side)

an excited state (-es N, the states of -mf) is the state that was number N at the first structure and is followed from structure to structure by the overlaps of its amplitudes, instead of the state number N in the order of the energies at every structure (calculators that hand out their states: the built-in GFN0-xTB and PySCF with a restricted reference; a state that is not found again with certainty is reported)

file with the Hessian the run starts from (Cartesian, Hartree/Bohr^2): a NumPy file, an ORCA .hess file, a Gaussian .fchk file or output, or numbers only (the square or its lower triangle); the first Hessian that is asked for is taken from it

xyz file of displacements (any length): a transition-state search (-order 1) takes the Hessian mode closest to it uphill and then tracks that mode by overlap, instead of the lowest mode (RS-I-RFO becomes its mode-following variant mf_rsirfo_*); for example the tangent of a chain at the image it starts from; Cartesian coordinates

coordinate system of the optimization: cart, ric, dic, tric (translation-rotation internal coordinates, delocalized), tric-p (their primitive set), tric-cart[:WEIGHT] (TRIC stacked with weighted Cartesian coordinates), spherical (every atom by r, theta, phi about the centroid), hyperspherical or polar (the whole structure by its distance from the centroid and 3N-1 angles; hyperspherical:FILE about the structure of FILE; for optimizations, not chains), auto (tric-cart, or cart for atom clusters, dense or periodic networks and very large systems), or a registered name. Calculators always receive Cartesian structures.

user-defined bias potentials as expressions of geometric variables in atomic units (energy in Hartree), e.g. '0.15*(dist(1,2)-1.5*ang)^2'; functions dist, angle, dihedral, oop, x, y, z with atoms or groups [1-3]; see the bias documentation

the spin state as the number of unpaired electrons 2S instead of -spin (2S + 1), as the 'spin' of PySCF, xTB's uhf, and several Rust engines count it; one value, or one per state. It sets the state only: an unrestricted reference for singlets is -u
program-specific calculator settings as key=value (Python literals), e.g. density_fit=True conv_tol=1e-10; for -os ase:module:Class they are constructor keywords

user-defined constraints as expressions in the -ubias language: 'EXPR' holds the starting value, 'EXPR = VALUE' a value (atomic units; 'ang', 'deg' convert), '; period = 2*pi' wraps angle-like functions, '; tolerance = 1e-8' holds a noisy function to that residual instead of 1e-10, e.g. 'dist(1,2) - dist(3,4)'; with -vc the functions of the cell as well, e.g. 'volume()', 'cell_a() = 10.5*ang', 'cell_a()/cell_b()'

groups of atoms (ex.) 1,2,3 4,5 whose distances to each other are held at their values in the input (MultiOptPy: 'set the gradient of internal coordinates between atoms to zero'): every distance of a group is a constraint as -pc bond is, taken out of the gradient and of the Hessian and restored after every step
CCQN reaction-coordinate axis from reactive bonds, as atom pairs (ex.) 1,2 3,4
CCQN axis toward the midpoint of the straight line to this product structure (xyz)
cosine of the CCQN cone half-angle (default: 0.1 for bonds, 0.5 for a product)
CCQN uphill step and initial saddle trust radius in Angstrom (default: 0.1)
vibrations at or below this wavenumber (cm^-1) are left out of the thermochemistry

treatment of the thermal energy of low frequencies apart from that of the entropy (-freq_corr): head-gordon, truhlar, or none; without it, the one that goes with -freq_corr (grimme: head-gordon, truhlar: truhlar)
cutoff (cm^-1) of the treatment of the thermal energy; without it, -freq_cutoff
concentration (mol/L) for the translational entropy of a solute instead of the pressure of the gas
scale factor of the vibrational frequencies in the thermochemistry
scale factor of the frequencies in the zero-point energy; without it, -freq_scale
imaginary frequencies up to this magnitude (cm^-1) enter the thermochemistry as real ones
moment of inertia that bounds the free rotor of -freq_corr grimme: global (1e-44 kg m^2) or molecule (the mean moment of the molecule)
distance (Bohr) within which atoms coincide in the point-group analysis
vibrational analysis: project the direction of the gradient out with the rigid-body motions (the modes orthogonal to a reaction path at a point that is not stationary)

after a converged optimization, the derivatives in every constant of the bias options (a force constant, an equilibrium value, the AFIR collision energy, ...; per unit of the option as it is written): of the bias energy, and how the stationary point and its energy without the bias move with the constant (dx/dp = -H^+ dg/dp with the Hessian of the whole surface); written to bias_derivatives.csv and the log

-mf opt_meci: do not check the branching plane with gradients at displaced structures when the search has converged (the check costs four evaluations of both states and sends the search on if the point is not stationary on the seam)

-mf opt_mesx, -mf opt_meci: what a step is judged by when the trust radius is adapted: energy (the change of the mean energy of the two states against the quadratic model of the projected gradient, as for a search on one surface) or merit (the change of the function the projected gradient belongs to: the mean energy within the seam and (E1 - E2)^2 / |g1 - g2|)

optimize the cell together with the atoms (cells periodic in three directions; the stress comes from the calculator, or from differences of the energy where it has none); with -es the stress of that state, with -mf the two states combined in the variables of the cell (their enthalpies and their gradients in the variables: crossing points and conical intersections with the cell)
-vc: external pressure in GPa; the enthalpy E + P V is minimized

-vc: artificial force on the cell (periodic AFIR): pairs of a collision energy in kJ/mol (positive: compress, negative: expand; a ramp as for -ma) and the distances it acts on, a list of a, b, c (origin to the tip of a lattice vector) and ab, bc, ca (between two tips), e.g. -vc_afir 200 a,b -vc_afir -100 ab

-vc: hard constraints on the cell, comma-separated, at the values of the input or NAME=VALUE: a, b, c (lengths, Angstrom), alpha, beta, gamma (degrees), volume (Angstrom^3; only the shape relaxes), shape (b/a, c/a and the three angles; only an isotropic scaling relaxes), a_vector, b_vector, c_vector (the three Cartesian components of a lattice vector, e.g. the normal vector of a slab), ax, ay, ..., cz (one component, Angstrom); the same constraints as -uc 'cell_a()', 'volume()', ...; e.g. -vc_fix volume, -vc_fix c_vector, -vc_fix a=10.5,gamma

-irc: further settings of the IRC as KEY=VALUE: first_step (check, the default: test the first point of each side and replace it by the energy minimum on a hypersphere around the transition state when it fails; off: MultiOptPy's first point), angle (largest angle in degrees between the downhill direction at the first point and the transition vector, 10), rho_min and rho_max (limits of actual over predicted energy change of the first step, 0.75 and 1.25), initial (mass-weighted length of the displacement from the transition state, 0.1 of the step size), sides (both, forward, backward), masses (standard: atomic weights, as the vibrational analysis; isotope: the most abundant isotopes, as MultiOptPy), energy_rise (retry, the default: a step that raised the energy is taken again at half its length, LQA and Euler; stop: end a side where the energy rises; off: keep such points, as MultiOptPy), overshoot (retry, the default, with energy_rise=retry: a step whose end has a gradient that points back along it is taken again at half its length; keep: such points stay), bend (off, the default; a share such as 0.25: no step is longer than the one that loses this share of the energy it gains by cutting the bend of the valley, from the curvature of the path and the Hessian across it; for exact Hessians along the path, -fc 1), approach (on, the default: below the force thresholds a side goes on to the minimum until the gradient is below approach_max_force and approach_rms_force, LQA, Euler, RK4; off: end at the first point below the thresholds, as MultiOptPy), approach_max_force (0.000015), approach_rms_force (0.00001), approach_steps (100), max_force (0.0004), rms_force (0.0001), min_points (10), oscillations (5), sphere_iterations (30), sphere_gradient (1e-4), sphere_step (1e-3)

-mf bitss REFERENCE: settings of the binary-image transition state search as KEY=VALUE: f (reduction of the separation per stage, 0.5), alpha (10), beta (0.1), interval (iterations between two settings of the coefficients, 100), points (points between the images for the barrier estimate, 3), min_separation (Bohr, 0.01), stages (30), step_share (longest step as a share of the separation asked for, 0.5; none: no limit), midpoint_shift (end when the midpoint moved by less than this share of the reduction of a stage; none), midpoint_gradient (true)
-vc: weight w of the lattice variables, gamma = w sqrt(number of atoms) (Gubler et al. 2023; values between 1 and 2 are recommended there)
show on the screen what the optimization methods do inside a step (the messages of the inner solvers, such as those of RS-I-RFO); they are always written to mopt.log
at convergence, check the Hessian and leave a stationary point that has more negative curvatures than -order asks for (0: a minimum), then go on; needs Hessians from the calculator
solver of the CCQN uphill subproblem: exact (global) or alm (the paper's method)

commands.name: run_kinetics
commands.feature: kinetics of reaction networks (rate constants, populations; RCMC among the solvers)

positional.name: json_file
positional.help: the network: reaction_network.json of run_mapper, its database reaction_network.sqlite (store=sqlite), or its run directory (the JSON file, or the database when the directory has only that), or MultiOptPy's network file

options.help: temperature (K)
the time of interest (s): the output time without --times and --time-grid, and the horizon of --priority, --sensitivity, --uncertainty (the last output time)
output times (s), e.g. 1e-9 1e-6 1e-3
TMIN TMAX N: N output times on a logarithmic grid (s)
node of the initial population (default: the node of the first input of a mapper run, node 0 of a network of MultiOptPy)
initial population over several nodes as ID:SHARE (normalized), e.g. 0:0.7 3:0.3
the run directory (populations.csv, rates.csv, rcmc_K_contracted.csv, rcmc_superstates.json, diagnostics.json, populations.svg, mopt.log, settings.json)
energies of the stationary points with --rate-theory eyring: electronic or free (the Gibbs energies of the file; stationary points without one are left out and listed)

propagate (contraction to superstates, then the exact propagation of their generator; no contraction where the time scales are not separated), rcmc (the published RCMC snapshot of Type A), legacy_rcmc (MultiOptPy's rcmc.py as it is), expm (the matrix exponential, the reference), spectral (eigenvectors of the symmetrized generator), steady (the stationary distribution), rosenbrock (the L-stable integrator ROS2, for mass_action and as a check), contract (the contraction of mass action of any reaction order, RCMC's extension: the fast species on their quasi-steady manifold, the rest propagated), windows (mass action by pseudo-first-order windows, each propagated by the contraction), kmc (kinetic Monte Carlo, Gillespie; small non-stiff models and semi_markov), or a registered name
reference time of a step of rcmc: gershgorin (ln 2 / sqrt(sigma rho) with the bounds of Iwata et al., as MultiOptPy), eigen (with the eigenvalues), diag (1 / |D_jj|)
propagate: the eliminated states must have relaxed (sigma t >= ln(1/tol)) and the separation ratio eps must not exceed it
propagate: a (G = D diag(1^T M)^-1, the RCMC superstates) or b (G = D M^-1)

eyring ((k_B T / h) exp(-dE / RT) with the energies of --energy-type), tst (free energies from the frequencies and structures of the states and saddle points, quasi-RRHO, symmetry numbers, the standard state), or rrkm (the Boltzmann average of RRKM k(E) from directly counted states, Beyer-Swinehart with classical rotors; the high-pressure limit of --model egme)

corrections of the flux of every step: wigner, bell (the infinite or the truncated parabola, --bell-truncation), eckart, skodje_truhlar (tunnelling from the imaginary frequency and the barriers), kappa (--kappa or a value per step of --annotations), landau_zener (crossings with a coupling; the double passage of a peaked or, with slope_product, a sloped crossing), zhu_nakamura (crossings with the slopes: sloped ones above the crossing energy; peaked ones from the higher minimum up, tunnelling below the crossing included), weak_coupling (the Airy form of the weak-coupling probability of a crossing with tunnelling below it; needs slope_product), cvt (canonical variational TST of the steps with a reaction path in --annotations; the others keep TST and say so), small_curvature and zero_curvature (tunnelling through the adiabatic barrier of path_profile.csv of freqmain -path, sct_profile_file), kramers (--friction or friction_s-1 per step), grote_hynes (a friction kernel: friction_memory_s or friction_kernel_file), reactive_flux (the transmission coefficient from trajectories of the saddle point, reactive_flux_kappa), collins_kimball (the diffusion limit of the bimolecular steps with --viscosity). Electron transfers are set per edge in --annotations (transfer)

bell: auto (the infinite parabola (u/2)/sin(u/2) where the truncation changes kappa by less than 1e-8, the parabola truncated at the barrier near and past u = 2 pi and for low barriers), on (always truncated), off (always infinite; refused at u >= 2 pi)

bell: the barrier that truncates the parabola: higher (from the higher minimum, the same factor from both sides, as skodje_truhlar), forward (from the first state of the step), reverse (from the second)
transmission coefficient of every step without its own

viscosity of the solvent (Pa s; water at 25 C: 8.9e-4) for the association of the barrierless dissociations into channels of the mapper: diffusion (Smoluchowski with Stokes-Einstein) and capture on contact in series (Collins-Kimball); without it the gas (capture on contact alone)
a saddle point below one of its minima: consistent (max(E_ts, E_a, E_b) for both directions, detailed balance kept), legacy (MultiOptPy: each direction by its own minimum), none

JSON file with data of nodes and edges by label or number: {"nodes": {"EQ3": {"frequencies_cm1": [...], "free_energy_hartree": ..., "symmetry_number": 2}}, "edges": {"TS12": {"kappa": 0.5, "coupling_cm1": 50, "gradient_difference": 0.02, "reduced_mass_amu": 10, "partner": "S", "partner_free_state": "EQ1"}, "TS4": {"transfer": "nonadiabatic", "reorganization_kcal_mol": 20, "coupling_cm1": 30}, "TS5": {"cvt_profile_file": "free_energy_profile.csv"}}, "species": {"S": {"energy_hartree": ..., "free_energy_hartree": ..., "frequencies_cm1": [...], "xyz": "...", "association": "factor:2"}}}

kinetic model: canonical (thermalized minima, first-order steps; bimolecular steps pseudo-first order at --concentration), mass_action (the states and the species as concentrations, non-linear, integrated by the solver rosenbrock; needs --total-concentration), auto (canonical where every bimolecular step is pseudo-first order, its partner changing by less than --order-tolerance with the states at --total-concentration; mass_action with the solver contract otherwise), egme (the energy-grained master equation with collisions; --rate-theory rrkm, --collision-model, --collision-frequency or --bath; phenomenological.csv), two_grain (hot intermediates as additional states; --cooling-rate), or semi_markov (gamma-distributed residence times of residence_shape in --annotations, or those of --md-trajectory; sampled by --solver kmc)

pressure of the standard state of the gas (Pa), as -press of freqmain: the translational entropy of tst, and the conversion RT ln(c R T / p) of the free energies of bimolecular steps to the standard concentration

the standard state of a solution (mol/L) instead of the gas, as -conc of freqmain: the free energies are taken there (tst computes them there) and it is the standard concentration of the bimolecular steps (default 1 mol/L, to which free energies of the gas are converted)

concentrations of the species of bimolecular steps as NAME:VALUE[UNIT] (mol/L by default; M, mM, uM, nM, pM, mol/m3, or a partial pressure in bar, atm, Pa): held fixed (pseudo-first order, k' = k2 [S]) with the model canonical, initial values with mass_action
species of bimolecular steps as NAME:E_HARTREE[:G_HARTREE] (electronic and free energy, '-' for none; or under "species" of --annotations with frequencies and structure)
bimolecular edges as EDGE:SPECIES:STATE (the edge takes up the species from its state STATE, where the species is free; or "partner" and "partner_free_state" of an edge of --annotations)

association entropy in solution: none (the conversion of the standard state only), wertz:F (every structure loses the fraction F of its translational and rotational entropy), free_volume:M:V or free_volume:SOLVENT (free volume of the solvent as GoodVibes), effective:C (an effective concentration in mol/L), factor:F
--model mass_action: the initial concentration of the states together (mol/L), shared by the initial population
--solver rosenbrock: relative tolerance of the step-size control
--rate-theory tst: low frequencies by grimme (interpolation to a free rotor), truhlar (raised to the cutoff), or none
--rate-theory tst: the cutoff of --qrrho (cm^-1)
--rate-theory tst: rotational symmetry numbers from the point groups (auto) or 1 (none), where the annotations give none
the level of a network of mopt-rs (1: exploration)

derivatives of the yields of these nodes (without a node: every state) at every output time and at t -> infinity with respect to the energy of every node (minima, transition states, crossings; 1/Hartree), ln k of every step (both directions together, so detailed balance holds; d ln p / d ln k is the degree of rate control), and the temperature (1/K), by forward-mode dual numbers through the solver (propagate, rcmc, expm, steady): sensitivity.csv; the degrees of rate control of the effective rate constants between superstates, which sum to 1: rate_control.csv
standard deviation (kcal/mol) of independent errors of the energies of the stationary points: quantiles of the populations at the last time over --samples draws, in uncertainty.csv
draws of --uncertainty
seed of the draws of --uncertainty and of the solver kmc

compare the populations with the matrix exponential and report the largest difference against TOL (default: the error estimate of the solver, max(eps_hat, exp(-sigma_hat t), 1e-10) for a contraction, 1e-10 otherwise)
rank the states for an exploration: population, max_population, residence, discovery_flux (priority.csv)
also report the populations of states with the same bond graph together (species.csv)
the relaxation rates of the generator and their gaps (spectrum.csv)

rank the refinement tasks (better energies of nodes and saddle points, the split of an N-furcation, the coupling of a crossing) by |d ln y / d theta| sigma for the populations of these nodes at the last output time (without a node: the most populated state); sigma from --uncertainty (1 kcal/mol without it) or uncertainty_kcal_mol in --annotations (refinement.csv)
kramers, grote_hynes: the friction on the reaction coordinate (1/s) of every saddle point without its own (friction_s-1 in --annotations)
rrkm, egme, two_grain: the width of the cells of the direct count of states (cm^-1)
egme: the width of the energy grains (cm^-1)
egme: the grains reach this many k_B T above the highest saddle point or well
egme: exponential_down (with --energy-transfer, detailed balance, normalized from the top grain down) or strong
egme, exponential_down: the mean energy transferred downwards in a collision (cm^-1)
egme: the collision frequency (1/s); without it the Lennard-Jones frequency at --pressure with --bath and --lennard-jones
egme: the bath gas as SIGMA:EPS:MASS (Angstrom, K, amu), e.g. 3.47:114:39.95 for argon
egme: SIGMA:EPS (Angstrom, K) of the molecule for every well without its own (lennard_jones in --annotations)
two_grain: the cooling rate of a hot intermediate (1/s; of the order of 1e11 to 1e12 in solution)
two_grain: a hot grain is added where H = k_exit(E*) / cooling rate exceeds this
kmc: the number of trajectories
kmc: the largest number of events of a run (more means the network is too stiff for kinetic Monte Carlo)
contract: species are eliminated while their effective loss rate times the output time exceeds this
windows: the largest relative change of a species over one pseudo-first-order window
--model auto: a bimolecular step is pseudo-first order when its partner changes by less than this (with the states at --total-concentration)

semi_markov: an XYZ trajectory whose frames are assigned to the minima of the network (bond graph, then RMSD; core sets): residence times and jumps for the model, and a Markov state model at --md-lag (msm.csv)
--md-trajectory: the time between two frames (fs)
--md-trajectory: the lag of the Markov state model (frames)
what the screen shows (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR); mopt.log has every message

commands.name: run_automecp
commands.feature: automated search for minimum-energy crossing points (MECP, MECI)

positional.name: input_file
positional.help: the structure the search starts from (xyz); it is minimized on its own state first

options.help: the settings file: step1_settings (the AFIR paths; the calculator, the charge and multiplicity of the first state), step2_settings (the optimization of the crossing points), step3_settings (the meta-IRC and the minimizations), each with the long option names of optmain, and manual_AFIR, state2, crossing_afir, mapper_settings
the AFIR pushes towards the crossing points, as -ma of optmain: triples of the force parameter (kJ/mol) and the atoms of two fragments, e.g. -ma 150 1,4 7,8

the second state: CHARGE MULTIPLICITY [ROOT] (root 0, the ground state of that multiplicity, when it is not given), e.g. -state2 0 3 for the crossing points with the triplet (MECP), -state2 0 1 1 with the first excited singlet (MECI); the first state is that of the input (electronic_charge, spin_multiplicity of step1_settings)

the root of the first state (0: the lowest state of its charge and multiplicity; default: excited_state of step1_settings, else 0), e.g. -root1 1 -state2 0 1 2 for the conical intersections of the first and the second excited singlet; a root here and another in step1_settings are refused
the kind of AFIR path: gp (the default, the force on the gradient projection of the two states), model (on the seam model function for an MECP, the Avoiding model function for an MECI), both

further settings of the mapper run as KEY=VALUE (the keys of run_mapper -map_opt, e.g. crossing_step=0.05); states, crossing_pushes, crossing_from, ts_states and crossing_afir are made by the command from its own options and are refused here; in mapper_settings of the settings file they must agree with them

the run directory: settings.json, mapper_config.json (the settings of the mapper run), automecp_summary.csv (one line per crossing point), and mapper/ (the run of the mapper: reaction_network.json, structures/, paths/, mapper_report.html, mopt.log)

commands.name: etmain
commands.feature: electron-transfer rate constants (EDEEL diabatic states, SAES, Marcus with Scher-Holstein tunnelling, Zhu-Nakamura)

options.help: edeel: the transfer within one molecule of donor, bridge, and acceptor by EDEEL's diabatic states, the crossings along the solvent coordinate of SAES, and the Marcus, Zhu-Nakamura, and Marcus-Levich-Jortner rates; hopping: the hop of a charge between two molecules (-et_donor, the molecule it starts on, and -et_acceptor), the transfer integral of the projection method at the input structure, the four-point reorganization energy from the equilibria of both molecules in both charges, and the Marcus rates both ways
the carrier of -et_method hopping: hole (between the highest occupied orbitals; the charged molecule one unit more positive) or electron (the lowest empty orbitals; one unit more negative)
the atoms of the donor (1-based; ranges such as 1-12,15): the species that holds the moving electron in the initial state
the atoms of the acceptor (as -et_donor)

auto: separate molecules when no bond joins the donor and the acceptor, else a molecule of donor, bridge (the other atoms), and acceptor, whose fragments (donor-bridge, bridge-acceptor) have their cut bonds capped by hydrogens; none; or the atoms of the bridge

the charges of the donor and the acceptor fragments without the moving electron (with their caps); the structure is the system with the moving electron. For -et_method hopping the charges of the two molecules without the carrier, and the structure is the pair in those charges

settings of -oniom as KEY=VALUE: low.KEY=VALUE and middle.KEY=VALUE (settings of the calculator of that level, which can be any calculator of -os, an ASE calculator among them: method, basis, and its own keys as -calc_opt takes them; -func, -bs, and -calc_opt belong to the highest level and are not handed down), link (scaled, the default: the link atom at the share g = (R(Q1) + R(H)) / (R(Q1) + R(Q2)) of the bond, as Gaussian; distance: at R(Q1) + R(H) from Q1, as MultiOptPy), high_charge and high_multiplicity, middle_charge and middle_multiplicity (the model systems; by default the charge of the whole structure and its multiplicity, changed by one where the link atoms change the parity of the electrons), embedding (mechanical, the default; electronic: the higher level of every region in the charges of the atoms around it, the Coulomb energy of the model with them taken off with the lower level), charges (lowest, the default: the lowest level's, the topology charges of GFN-FF; or FILE: one per atom, in e), boundary (rc, the default: the charge of each Q2 moved to the midpoints of its bonds to the environment; zero; keep), micro (on by default: optmain, ircmain, and the chains of nebmain move the core, the outermost model region and the outer atoms of its links, and relax the rest on the lowest level (with electronic embedding the whole surface) to a minimum before every evaluation; Hessians are those of the core; the files hold the whole system; off: every atom moves), micro_mode_kill (off, the default: the environment, the low layer, is not mode-killed, the core is by its optimizer; N: the check for negative curvature of the environment after the first and every Nth relaxation, its modes followed down), micro_curvature (guided, the default: the check starts from the softest mode of the last one and takes the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxation as preconditioner; plain: from a fixed start without one), micro_precondition (lindh2007d3, the default, or another model Hessian of -modelhess, or none: its block of the environment, built at the free atoms and the fixed atoms within 4 Angstrom of the environment and shifted by micro_precondition_shift, default 1e-3 Hartree/Bohr^2, is the initial matrix of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations and the preconditioner of the curvature check; up to 16 are kept, one per structure they were built near; environments of at most 6000 variables; a relaxation that fails with it is made again without it), micro_tolerance (largest gradient component of the relaxed environment; by default micro_tolerance_factor times the thresholds of the forces of the run itself, the largest force and the RMS force of its criteria; a relaxation whose line search fails goes on with FIRE, one that ends above its tolerance says so), micro_tolerance_factor (1, the default, or a smaller share such as 0.1 of the thresholds of the forces of the run to which the environment is relaxed, not below 1e-5; up to 1), micro_check_tolerance (largest gradient component of the environment, Hartree/Bohr, for every Hessian of a check of stability: the verification of a converged saddle-point search, the start of an IRC, the stationary points of the mapper, a vibrational analysis; 1e-5 by default, never looser than the relaxations of the run; an environment that stands on a saddle point of its own is moved off it and relaxed again before any Hessian, and the error of the curvatures of a check is estimated by moving the environment to the minimum of its quadratic model and taking the Hessian again), micro_correct (on, the default, or off: correct the energy and the core gradient for the gradient left in the environment by the response of the newest Hessian of the core, where that moves the environment by at most 0.05 Bohr), micro_core_shell (Angstrom: the free atoms of the environment within that distance of the model region are moved by the optimizer with the core; by default none), micro_hessian (effective, the default: the Hessian of the relaxed surface; approximate: the same with the inverse of the limited-memory BFGS of the relaxations; held: the core block with the environment held), micro_hessian_solve (auto, the default: the response of the environment from its dense block, by the analytic Hessian of the lowest level or central differences of its gradient, where that costs fewer gradients than conjugate gradients and fits in the memory, conjugate gradients otherwise; dense; cg), micro_hessian_memory (GiB the Hessian of the core may take, by default half of the free memory: the analytic Hessian of the whole system where its matrices fit, central differences otherwise, refused where those do not fit either), micro_hessian_shell (Angstrom: only the environment within that distance of the core responds in the Hessian of the core, the rest is held; by default all of it), micro_optimizer (lbfgs, the default; tn: truncated Newton; or a method of -opt, for environments of at most 500 atoms), micro_coord (cart, the default; fragments: translation, rotation, and internal coordinates of each fragment of the environment), micro_predict (on or off, the default: start each relaxation from the predicted response of the environment), micro_adaptive (0, the default; ETA: the tolerance of a relaxation ETA times the largest core gradient while that is large, and a last relaxation to the full tolerance at the end), micro_replicas (1, the default: one environment; K: K replicas of the environment, each relaxed from its own environment of the core before, combined into the soft minimum -kT ln sum_k exp(-E_k / kT) of their surfaces, whose gradient is the weighted mean of theirs; not a free energy, at most kT ln K below the lowest replica; the files hold the lowest replica and NAME_replicas.xyz all of them), micro_replica_temperature (K of the soft minimum, 298.15 by default), micro_replica_start (perturb, the default: every free atom of the first relaxed environment moved by micro_replica_amplitude, 0.05 Angstrom, in a random direction of seed micro_replica_seed, 1; md: after micro_replica_md_steps, 200, steps of molecular dynamics of the environment at the temperature with the core held; files: the environments of the last K whole structures of micro_replica_files, such as the NAME_replicas.xyz of a run with replicas), traj_high_only (on or off, default off: write only the real high-layer atoms to optimization, MD and mapper XYZ trajectories)

test the SCF solution for instabilities every N evaluations and go on from a stabler one where it is unstable, repeating the evaluation there (0, the default: never; programs with an SCF that can test it, such as PySCF; the others say so once)

with -stability: an instability towards another kind of wavefunction (restricted to unrestricted): report (the default: it is said, the kind is kept), switch (go on with the unrestricted kind for the rest of the run), off (not tested)

how many structures are calculated at the same time where a command has several that do not depend on each other (the images of a chain, the two structures of a search between two structures, the states of a function of several states): the threads of the command for the built-in calculators, copies in worker processes for the calculators of the Python side. -core stays the threads of one calculation (0: as many structures at a time as -core has threads for the built-in calculators, one for those of the Python side)

an excited state (-es N, the states of -mf) is the state that was number N at the first structure and is followed from structure to structure by the overlaps of its amplitudes, instead of the state number N in the order of the energies at every structure (calculators that hand out their states: the built-in GFN0-xTB and PySCF with a restricted reference; a state that is not found again with certainty is reported)

file with the Hessian the run starts from (Cartesian, Hartree/Bohr^2): a NumPy file, an ORCA .hess file, a Gaussian .fchk file or output, or numbers only (the square or its lower triangle); the first Hessian that is asked for is taken from it

xyz file of displacements (any length): a transition-state search (-order 1) takes the Hessian mode closest to it uphill and then tracks that mode by overlap, instead of the lowest mode (RS-I-RFO becomes its mode-following variant mf_rsirfo_*); for example the tangent of a chain at the image it starts from; Cartesian coordinates

coordinate system of the optimization: cart, ric, dic, tric (translation-rotation internal coordinates, delocalized), tric-p (their primitive set), tric-cart[:WEIGHT] (TRIC stacked with weighted Cartesian coordinates), spherical (every atom by r, theta, phi about the centroid), hyperspherical or polar (the whole structure by its distance from the centroid and 3N-1 angles; hyperspherical:FILE about the structure of FILE; for optimizations, not chains), auto (tric-cart, or cart for atom clusters, dense or periodic networks and very large systems), or a registered name. Calculators always receive Cartesian structures.

user-defined bias potentials as expressions of geometric variables in atomic units (energy in Hartree), e.g. '0.15*(dist(1,2)-1.5*ang)^2'; functions dist, angle, dihedral, oop, x, y, z with atoms or groups [1-3]; see the bias documentation

the spin state as the number of unpaired electrons 2S instead of -spin (2S + 1), as the 'spin' of PySCF, xTB's uhf, and several Rust engines count it; one value, or one per state. It sets the state only: an unrestricted reference for singlets is -u
program-specific calculator settings as key=value (Python literals), e.g. density_fit=True conv_tol=1e-10; for -os ase:module:Class they are constructor keywords

user-defined constraints as expressions in the -ubias language: 'EXPR' holds the starting value, 'EXPR = VALUE' a value (atomic units; 'ang', 'deg' convert), '; period = 2*pi' wraps angle-like functions, '; tolerance = 1e-8' holds a noisy function to that residual instead of 1e-10, e.g. 'dist(1,2) - dist(3,4)'; with -vc the functions of the cell as well, e.g. 'volume()', 'cell_a() = 10.5*ang', 'cell_a()/cell_b()'

groups of atoms (ex.) 1,2,3 4,5 whose distances to each other are held at their values in the input (MultiOptPy: 'set the gradient of internal coordinates between atoms to zero'): every distance of a group is a constraint as -pc bond is, taken out of the gradient and of the Hessian and restored after every step
CCQN reaction-coordinate axis from reactive bonds, as atom pairs (ex.) 1,2 3,4
CCQN axis toward the midpoint of the straight line to this product structure (xyz)
cosine of the CCQN cone half-angle (default: 0.1 for bonds, 0.5 for a product)
CCQN uphill step and initial saddle trust radius in Angstrom (default: 0.1)
vibrations at or below this wavenumber (cm^-1) are left out of the thermochemistry

treatment of the thermal energy of low frequencies apart from that of the entropy (-freq_corr): head-gordon, truhlar, or none; without it, the one that goes with -freq_corr (grimme: head-gordon, truhlar: truhlar)
cutoff (cm^-1) of the treatment of the thermal energy; without it, -freq_cutoff
concentration (mol/L) for the translational entropy of a solute instead of the pressure of the gas
scale factor of the vibrational frequencies in the thermochemistry
scale factor of the frequencies in the zero-point energy; without it, -freq_scale
imaginary frequencies up to this magnitude (cm^-1) enter the thermochemistry as real ones
moment of inertia that bounds the free rotor of -freq_corr grimme: global (1e-44 kg m^2) or molecule (the mean moment of the molecule)
distance (Bohr) within which atoms coincide in the point-group analysis
vibrational analysis: project the direction of the gradient out with the rigid-body motions (the modes orthogonal to a reaction path at a point that is not stationary)

after a converged optimization, the derivatives in every constant of the bias options (a force constant, an equilibrium value, the AFIR collision energy, ...; per unit of the option as it is written): of the bias energy, and how the stationary point and its energy without the bias move with the constant (dx/dp = -H^+ dg/dp with the Hessian of the whole surface); written to bias_derivatives.csv and the log

-mf opt_meci: do not check the branching plane with gradients at displaced structures when the search has converged (the check costs four evaluations of both states and sends the search on if the point is not stationary on the seam)

-mf opt_mesx, -mf opt_meci: what a step is judged by when the trust radius is adapted: energy (the change of the mean energy of the two states against the quadratic model of the projected gradient, as for a search on one surface) or merit (the change of the function the projected gradient belongs to: the mean energy within the seam and (E1 - E2)^2 / |g1 - g2|)

optimize the cell together with the atoms (cells periodic in three directions; the stress comes from the calculator, or from differences of the energy where it has none); with -es the stress of that state, with -mf the two states combined in the variables of the cell (their enthalpies and their gradients in the variables: crossing points and conical intersections with the cell)
-vc: external pressure in GPa; the enthalpy E + P V is minimized

-vc: artificial force on the cell (periodic AFIR): pairs of a collision energy in kJ/mol (positive: compress, negative: expand; a ramp as for -ma) and the distances it acts on, a list of a, b, c (origin to the tip of a lattice vector) and ab, bc, ca (between two tips), e.g. -vc_afir 200 a,b -vc_afir -100 ab

-vc: hard constraints on the cell, comma-separated, at the values of the input or NAME=VALUE: a, b, c (lengths, Angstrom), alpha, beta, gamma (degrees), volume (Angstrom^3; only the shape relaxes), shape (b/a, c/a and the three angles; only an isotropic scaling relaxes), a_vector, b_vector, c_vector (the three Cartesian components of a lattice vector, e.g. the normal vector of a slab), ax, ay, ..., cz (one component, Angstrom); the same constraints as -uc 'cell_a()', 'volume()', ...; e.g. -vc_fix volume, -vc_fix c_vector, -vc_fix a=10.5,gamma

-irc: further settings of the IRC as KEY=VALUE: first_step (check, the default: test the first point of each side and replace it by the energy minimum on a hypersphere around the transition state when it fails; off: MultiOptPy's first point), angle (largest angle in degrees between the downhill direction at the first point and the transition vector, 10), rho_min and rho_max (limits of actual over predicted energy change of the first step, 0.75 and 1.25), initial (mass-weighted length of the displacement from the transition state, 0.1 of the step size), sides (both, forward, backward), masses (standard: atomic weights, as the vibrational analysis; isotope: the most abundant isotopes, as MultiOptPy), energy_rise (retry, the default: a step that raised the energy is taken again at half its length, LQA and Euler; stop: end a side where the energy rises; off: keep such points, as MultiOptPy), overshoot (retry, the default, with energy_rise=retry: a step whose end has a gradient that points back along it is taken again at half its length; keep: such points stay), bend (off, the default; a share such as 0.25: no step is longer than the one that loses this share of the energy it gains by cutting the bend of the valley, from the curvature of the path and the Hessian across it; for exact Hessians along the path, -fc 1), approach (on, the default: below the force thresholds a side goes on to the minimum until the gradient is below approach_max_force and approach_rms_force, LQA, Euler, RK4; off: end at the first point below the thresholds, as MultiOptPy), approach_max_force (0.000015), approach_rms_force (0.00001), approach_steps (100), max_force (0.0004), rms_force (0.0001), min_points (10), oscillations (5), sphere_iterations (30), sphere_gradient (1e-4), sphere_step (1e-3)

-mf bitss REFERENCE: settings of the binary-image transition state search as KEY=VALUE: f (reduction of the separation per stage, 0.5), alpha (10), beta (0.1), interval (iterations between two settings of the coefficients, 100), points (points between the images for the barrier estimate, 3), min_separation (Bohr, 0.01), stages (30), step_share (longest step as a share of the separation asked for, 0.5; none: no limit), midpoint_shift (end when the midpoint moved by less than this share of the reduction of a stage; none), midpoint_gradient (true)
-vc: weight w of the lattice variables, gamma = w sqrt(number of atoms) (Gubler et al. 2023; values between 1 and 2 are recommended there)
show on the screen what the optimization methods do inside a step (the messages of the inner solvers, such as those of RS-I-RFO); they are always written to mopt.log
at convergence, check the Hessian and leave a stationary point that has more negative curvatures than -order asks for (0: a minimum), then go on; needs Hessians from the calculator
solver of the CCQN uphill subproblem: exact (global) or alm (the paper's method)
